6.en: Operations. Gr. enerḡemata, “workings,” from energeō, “to be at work,” “to be in action,” “to operate.” Our word “energy” comes from this root. In the NT, energēmata, occurs only here and in v. 10. The word probably refers to the divine energizings operating in the church and perhaps in all nature. Same God. Having introduced the Spirit and the Son in vs. 4, 5, Paul here completes his mention of the three persons of the Godhead by referring to the Father as the originator and sustainer of all the manifold endowments and workings of the spiritual powers that He has provided for the effectual accomplishment of the work of His church. There are various “gifts,” “administrations,” and “operations,” but all proceed from one God, one Lord, one Spirit, that is, from Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
6.zh:
功用也有分別，神卻是一位，在眾人裡面運行一切的事。

**功用。**energemata，源於energeo，“工作”，“運行”，“起作用”。英語的energy（能量）即來自這個詞根。在《新約》中，energemata只出現在本節和本章第10節，可能指上帝的能力在教會或大自然中的運行。
**上帝卻是一位。**保羅在4,5節中介紹了聖靈和聖子，在本節稱聖父是祂在教會中所賜各樣屬靈職任，能力和恩賜的源頭和維持者，以有效地完成祂教會的工作。這樣，三位一體的上帝他都提到了。“恩賜”，“職任”和“功用”雖有不同，但都來自一位上帝，一位主，一個靈，就是聖父，聖子和聖靈。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷九第145頁。

5.en: Administrations. Gr. diakoniai, “ministrations,” “services” (see Rom. 15:31). The word is often translated “ministry” (see Acts 1:17, 25; 6:4; 20:24; Rom. 12:7; 1:12). There are different kinds of services in the church, but all are controlled by one Lord. Lord. In the NT this term standing by itself generally refers to Christ. It is one of the names by which He was known among the disciples (John 20:25). The purpose of this verse seems to be to establish the fact that all the various forms of ministry in the church originated with Christ. Because of this, and because all the kinds of ministrations are necessary, no individual should be unduly proud of his particular appointment to a responsible position in the church; nor should anyone feel disappointed because he has been assigned to a humble post of duty (cf. Matt. 23:8; 1 Peter 5:2, 3).
5.zh:
職事也有分別，主卻是一位。

**職事。**diakoniai，“服侍”，“服務”（見羅15:31）。該詞常譯為“職任”（見徒1:17,25；6:4；20:24；羅12:7）。教會中有不同的職任，但都是由同一位主掌管的。
**主。**在《新約》中通常指基督。這是門徒對祂的稱呼之一（約20:25）。本節的目的似乎是要明確教會中的各種職任都來自基督。正因為如此，也正因為各種職任都是需要的，任何人都不可為自己在教會中所擔任的特別職任而驕傲，也不要為被分配到一個卑微的崗位上而感到失望（參太23:8；彼前5:2,3）。

8.en: Word of wisdom. That is, the utterance of wisdom. A man possessed of this gift was not only wise, he was able also to explain his wisdom to others. For a definition of wisdom and for the contrast between wisdom and knowledge see on Prov. 1:2. Word of knowledge. That is, utterance of knowledge. Knowledge, generally speaking, is man’s ability to apprehend facts. In relation to the gospel it would be his ability to apprehend spiritual truth and arrange it in an orderly manner for presentation to others. This apprehension of truth comes from the study of the Scriptures, or directly from God by inspiration. The “word of knowledge” is therefore the power to discourse on those truths, presenting them in proper order to the minds of the hearers so that they would be convinced of what they hear.
8.zh:
這人蒙聖靈賜他智慧的言語，那人也蒙這位聖靈賜他知識的言語，

**智慧的言語。**擁有這種恩賜的人不僅智慧，而且能向別人解釋他的智慧。關於智慧的定義和智慧與知識的區別，見箴1:2註釋。
**知識的言語。**一般說來，知識就是人領會事實的能力。就福音而言，知識就是他理解屬靈真理、並有條理地向別人講述的能力。這種對真理的領會來自研究聖經，或上帝聖靈的直接啟示。所以“知識的言語”就是講述這些真理的能力，將真理條理分明地展現給聽眾，使他們能相信所聽到的話。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–9節）**。《證言》卷九第144頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–11節）**。《基督比喻實訓》第327頁；《今日的生活》第37頁。

13.en: Baptized into one body. The baptism here referred to is doubtless that which accompanies baptism by water in the case of every truly newborn child of God (see Matt. 3:11). Water baptism is valueless unless the one being baptized has been born again by the Holy Spirit (John 3:5, 6, 8). It is through the work of the Holy Spirit that men become members of the body of Christ. Jews or Gentiles. Whatever may have been a man’s former condition of life, or whatever his nationality, surrender to Christ and baptism by His Spirit removes all former differences between him and other believers, for all are on the same level in the sight of God. It is not nationality that counts, but humble acceptance of Jesus as Saviour, and willingness to let Him lead at all times. Bond or free. Or, “slaves and freedmen.” Compare Gal. 3:28; Col. 3:11. The fact that there were many nationalities and social classes comprising the body of Christ, heightens the idea of diversity. Yet in spite of diversity there is unity. Into one Spirit. Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the omission of the preposition “into.” Without it the phrase reads, “of one Spirit.” The reference is probably to the work of the Holy Spirit at the time of baptism, including the bestowal of the gifts. Some commentators refer this phrase “all made to drink” to the common participation in the cup at the Lord’s Supper, by which action believers showed that they all belonged to the same body, the church of God, and were all united in heart. However, the form of the verb translated “made to drink” is such as to refer the action of drinking to a definite time in the past, rather than to repeated participations in the ordinance of the Lord’s Supper.
13.zh:
我們不拘是猶太人，是希利尼人，是為奴的，是自主的，都從一位聖靈受洗，成了一個身體，飲於一位聖靈。

**不拘是猶太人，是希臘人。**人不論以前的生活狀況如何，屬於什麼國籍，只要降服於基督，接受聖靈的洗禮，就消除了他原先同其他信徒之間的一切差異，因為在上帝眼中，人人都是平等的。重要的不是國籍，而在於謙卑地接受耶穌為救主，並願意時刻讓祂來領導。
**是為奴的，是自主的。**或“奴隸與自由民”。參加3:28；西3:11。基督的身體是又許多國籍和社會階層的人所組成的。他們之間存在很大的差異。儘管這樣，他們仍是團結一致的。
**從一位聖靈。**可能指受洗時聖靈的工作，包括賜予聖靈的恩賜。有些解經家認為“飲於”是指信徒共同領受聖餐的杯，以此表明他們屬於同一個身體，就是上帝的教會，並且同心合意。但動詞“飲於”指過去某一次的飲用，不是指聖餐禮的反覆飲用。
**受洗，成了一個身體。**這裡的受洗無疑指每一個真正新生的上帝兒女所受水的洗禮（見太3:11）。人若不經過聖靈的重生，水的洗禮就毫無意義（約3:5,6,8）。藉著聖靈的工作，人才能成為基督身上的肢體。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第25頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–21節）**。《使徒行述》第317頁。

12.en: The body is one. The human body is one organism, but it is composed of various members and parts, each having its own indispensable function, and all uniting harmoniously in one whole. Though the different parts of the body are separate and distinct in their shape, size, and functions, they are all essential, and all unite in making up the entire body, and are all under the same guiding power, the head. Christ. The apostle represents the church as the body of Christ, signifying that it is one united body, with Christ as its head (see 1 Cor. 12:27; Eph. 1:22, 23; Col. 1:18–24). By a figure of speech a part is here made to represent the whole. Christ, the head of the church, stands for the entire church. All the members of the church are separate individuals, having varying offices and responsibilities in the church. For these tasks they receive gifts from God appropriate to their individual needs, but they all are answerable to Christ and are united in Him.
12.zh:
就如身子是一個，卻有許多肢體；而且肢體雖多，仍是一個身子；基督也是這樣。

**身子是一個。**人體是一個有機體，由不同的肢體組成。它們各司其職，互相配合成為一個整體。雖然身體不同的肢體形狀、大小和功能都不同，但都很重要。它們結合成為一個完整的身體，受同一個力量所支配，那就是大腦。
**基督。**使徒把教會比作基督的身體，說明教會是統一的整體，基督是她的頭（見林前12:27；弗1:22,23；西1:18-24）。這裡用局部代表整體。以教會的元首基督代表整個教會。所有教會的成員都是各司其職的個人。為此他們根據個人的需要領受上帝的恩賜。但他們都要對基督負責，並在祂裡面合而為一。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》第413，466頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–27節）**。《證言》卷七第174頁。

7.en: Manifestation of the Spirit. This may be understood either as a manifestation that the Spirit gives or as a manifestation that reveals the Holy Spirit in His true nature and operations. The meaning is not too different. The reference is to spiritual gifts, which were manifestations produced by the Spirit, and at the same time manifestations that revealed the character and work of the Spirit. To every man. That is, every Christian. It appears that the gifts in the early church were widely if not universally distributed among the various members. However, the phrase “to every man” may simply mean, to every man to whom a special gift is given. To profit withal. That is, for the common good or advantage of the church as a whole, though personal benefit is not excluded (see ch. 14:4, 12). The gifts are imparted according to the needs of the church in special situations. In the wisdom of God the church at Corinth received a liberal endowment of gifts (ch. 1:7). The supernatural manifestations confirmed the faith of the early believers, who had not the historical evidence of the power of Christianity that men possess today. Nor had they trained and experienced leadership or men skilled in the Word of God. Bibles, consisting of only the OT, were rare. To supply the lack and to meet the need, supernatural gifts were liberally bestowed.
7.zh:
聖靈顯在各人身上，是叫人得益處。

**聖靈顯在。**可以理解為聖靈的顯示，或表顯聖靈的真正性質和運行。其含義沒有太大的區別，都是指屬靈的恩賜，既是聖靈的表顯，同時也顯示了聖靈的性質和工作。
**各人。**就是每一個基督徒。在早期教會中，聖靈的恩賜即使不是信徒中間普遍存在，也是分佈廣泛的。但“各人”可能只是指每一個賦有特別恩賜的人。
**得益處。**指為了教會整體的利益，當然也包括個人的利益（見14:4,12）。恩賜是根據教會在特殊情況下的需要而賜下的。本著上帝的智慧，哥林多教會得到了豐富的恩賜（1:7）。這超自然的表現證明了早期信徒的信心。他們並沒有現代的人所擁有的基督教能力的歷史證據，也沒有訓練有素，經驗豐富的領袖或精通上帝之道的人。聖經很少，只有《舊約》。為了彌補缺欠，滿足需要，就豐富地賜下了超自然的恩賜。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第364頁。

26.en: Suffer. When injury comes to one member of the body, the whole body is caused to suffer, because of the natural, vital connection between the injured member and the rest of the body. So with the church; there should be such close and living connection among the members that the suffering of one is communicated to the entire church, and the interest and active help of all is enlisted to help the suffering member. If one is suffering through poverty, for example, it is the responsibility of the church to relieve that suffering by ministry to his material needs; if one is persecuted for his faith, the whole body of believers should share his trial and rally round him to give what support they can (see Rom. 12:13, 15, 16; Gal. 6:2; 7T 292). The church is a closely knit organization; in it is to be seen unity that is likened to that between the members of the Godhead (John 17:21, 23; Rom. 12:4, 5). Christ identifies Himself with His people, and when one of them suffers He feels the pain (Matt. 25:40, 45; Acts 9:5). As in the natural body a sting in a finger is felt right up the arm and through the body, so in the spiritual body, when one of Satan’s poisoned darts pierces the heart of one member, the whole church is affected. The whole body is disgraced by the defection of the least member. Honoured. The health of one member of the body is reflected in the well-being of the entire body. So in the church. The honor that comes to one of its members by special endowment is shared by all, for all are benefited by his special endowments.
26.zh:
若一個肢體受苦，所有的肢體就一同受苦；若一個肢體得榮耀，所有的肢體就一同快樂。

**受苦。**當身體的某一個肢體受到傷害時，全身都會因而受苦，因為受傷的肢體與身體的其他部位有著天然而重要的聯繫。教會也是這樣。肢體之間應當有這種緊密活潑的聯繫，這樣，一個肢體的痛苦會傳遞到整個教會，大家都關心並積極幫助那受苦的肢體。例如，一個肢體若遭受貧窮，教會就有責任藉著幫助他物質的需要而減輕他的痛苦。如果一個肢體因信仰受逼迫，所有的信徒就都應分擔他的試煉並儘可能地支援他（見羅12:13,15,16；加6:2；《教會證言》卷七292頁）。教會是一個緊密結合的組織，就像三一真神之間的聯合一樣（約17:21,23；羅12:4,5）。基督將自己與祂的子民視為一體。他們中若有一個人受苦，祂都能感受得到（太25:40,45；徒9:5）。就像身體的一個手指被刺，整個手臂乃至於全身都會感受到疼痛，屬靈的身體也是如此。當撒但的毒箭射到一個肢體的心臟時，整個教會都會受到影響。整個身體會因最小肢體的缺陷而蒙羞。
**榮耀。**身體中一個肢體的健康反映了全身的健康。教會也是這樣。因特殊的恩賜臨到其某一個肢體的榮耀，是為大家所共享的，因為所有的人都受惠於他特殊的恩賜。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷七第292頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–27節）**。《論福利工作》第23頁。

11.en: Selfsame Spirit. All the various endowments of power supplied to the church are imparted by the Holy Spirit, who works in and through the believers. Since God controls the working of the gifts of the Spirit, it is safe to conclude that they must all be in perfect harmony with His overall plan for the finishing of His work on earth. The knowledge that all the gifts come from God should be enough to forbid any display of pride in their possession. Every man. See on v. 7. Similarly today, all who surrender to Christ and become members of His church on earth, no matter what their nationality or social or economic status or intellectual attainments, have the assurance that the Holy Spirit will equip them with ability to perform their Christian duties with a high degree of effectiveness (see DA 823). As he will. The Holy Spirit distributes His gifts to believers in accordance with His knowledge of their capacities and the needs existing in the experience of each individual. It is not an arbitrary division, but one based on supreme knowledge and understanding. The great objective of preparing the church to meet God without spot or fault at the coming of Christ is the controlling factor in the distribution of the gifts (see Eph. 4:12, 13; 5:27; Rev. 14:5). This statement that the gifts are imparted to each one as the Holy Spirit sees most needful is a source of encouragement to believers. It assures them that they will receive exactly the ability and strength that they need in order to live godly lives and in order to witness powerfully under whatever circumstances they may be placed. The personality of the Holy Spirit is revealed in this verse, for the acts of distributing gifts to men as He sees best for their own and the church’s interests, relate definitely to a person. The Spirit’s sovereignty is also proved here, because He distributes the gifts entirely as He pleases.
11.zh:
這一切都是這位聖靈所運行、隨己意分給各人的。

**這位聖靈。**是聖靈把各樣的能力賜給教會。聖靈在信徒心中運行並藉著他們工作。由於上帝掌管著聖靈恩賜的工作，我們完全有把握說，這一切恩賜肯定是與上帝完成祂地上聖工的整體計劃完全和諧的。認識到所有的恩賜來自上帝，足以防止擁有者任何驕傲的表現。
**隨己意。**聖靈把祂的恩賜分給信徒，是根據祂對他們能力的瞭解和個人的實際需要。這不是任意的分配，而是依據至高的認識和理解。分配恩賜的動機就是預備教會在基督來臨時毫無瑕疵地迎見上帝這個偉大的目標（見弗4:12,13；5:27；啟14:5）。按照聖靈所視為最需要將恩賜分給各人，這句話是信徒鼓舞的一泉源。這就向他們保證，他們將會得到所需要的能力敬虔度日，在任何環境中作出有力的見證。
本節體現了聖靈的位格，因為採取行動按照信徒和教會的最高利益分配恩賜的，肯定是一個有位格的神。這裡也證明了聖靈的主權，因為祂完全按照自己的意思分配恩賜。
**各人。**見第7節註釋。今天也一樣，凡降服基督並加入祂地上教會的人，不論其國籍、社會和經濟地位，或知識造詣，都有把握得到聖靈的能力，以高效履行基督徒的責任（見《歷代願望》823頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第315頁；《歷代願望》第823頁。

9.en: Faith. The faith here spoken of is not that which all Christians possess. It is a special kind of faith such as enables its possessor to do exceptional exploits for God (see Matt. 17:20; 21:21; 1 Cor. 13:2). Gifts of healing. Special powers are here indicated such as those exercised by the apostles (Mark 16:18; Acts 3:2–8; 14:8–10; etc.). It is, of course, the privilege of all to request healing for the sick and to receive answers to prayer. But this is to be distinguished from the “gifts of healing” here spoken of. It appears that those with this gift possessed divine knowledge and direction in their work, and healed only those whom God directed them to heal. They thus possessed certain knowledge of the outcome.
9.zh:
又有一人蒙這位聖靈賜他信心，還有一人蒙這位聖靈賜他醫病的恩賜，

**信心。**這裡所說的信心並不是全體基督徒所擁有的信心，而是一種特殊的信心，例如能使擁有者為上帝施行奇蹟的信心（見太17:20；21:21；林前13:2）。
**醫病的恩賜。**這裡所指的是使徒們所擁有的那種特殊能力（可16:18；徒3:2-8；14:8-10等）。當然，所有的人都有祈求疾病得醫治，禱告得回應的權利。但這與本節所說的“醫病的恩賜”不同。擁有這種恩賜的人在工作中似乎有上帝的知識和指引，只醫治上帝指示他們醫治的人。所以他們對結果有一定的把握。

10.en: Working of miracles. As in the case of “gifts of healing” (see on v. 9) this was a special gift performed under divine direction. However, it is the privilege of those not possessing the gift to pray for miraculous intervention and to have their prayers answered if God so chooses. Prophecy. This is the power to speak authoritatively for God, or on God’s behalf, either by foretelling future events or by declaring God’s will for the present (see Ex. 3:10, 14, 15; Deut. 18:15, 18; 2 Sam. 23:2; Matt. 11:9, 10; 2 Peter 1:21). Prophecy is the means chosen by God to establish communication between Himself and man (see Num. 12:6; Amos 3:7). The whole Bible has come to men by means of this gift (see 2 Tim. 3:16; 2 Peter 1:20, 21). Scriptures testify of Jesus, and the gift of prophecy is appropriately called the “testimony of Jesus” (Rev. 19:10; see John 5:39; Rev. 12:17). Visions, dreams, special divine illumination of mind, are ways in which this gift of prophecy works (see Num. 12:6; Rev. 1:1–3). Thus the human agent becomes the mouthpiece of God (see 2 Sam. 23:2; Matt. 3:3; 2 Peter 1:21). God intended that this important gift of the Spirit should be with His church to the end of time (see Joel 2:28, 29; Rev. 12:17; 19:10). In fact, it is to be a mark of identification of God’s true church in the last days (Rev. 12:17; 19:10). This is only reasonable, because God has been using this channel through which to reveal Himself and impart His messages to the world ever since the fall of Adam. Discerning of spirits. This is the ability to distinguish between divine and counterfeit inspiration (see 1 John 4:1–3; TM 228, 229). Christ warned His church that false prophets would arise, particularly in the last days, and all should be on the alert to recognize and reject such false teachers (see Matt. 24:4, 5, 11, 23–25). The apostles in the early church had the ability to distinguish between true and false preachers and professors of Christianity (see Acts 5:1–10; 13:9–11). There was need for this gift in the early days of the church, when there were doubtless many pretenders to possession of these gifts. Satan has ever been ready to counterfeit the true, and often supports the false claims of pretenders by supernatural miracles (2 Thess. 2:9; Rev. 13:13, 14). Kinds of tongues. This gift is discussed at length in ch. 14, where it is contrasted with the gift of prophecy. Interpretation of tongues. A special gift was needed to interpret the messages imparted (see ch. 14:27, 28; Additional Note on Chapter 14).
10.zh:
又叫一人能行異能，又叫一人能作先知，又叫一人能辨別諸靈，又叫一人能說方言，又叫一人能翻方言。

**行異能。**和“醫病的恩賜”（見第9節註釋）一樣，這也是一種在上帝的指導下行使的特殊恩賜。但如果上帝願意的話，沒有這種恩賜的人也有權祈求神蹟的介入，應允他們的祈禱。
**作先知。**這是奉上帝的權威，代表上帝說話的能力，預言將來的事件，宣佈上帝目前的旨意（見出3:10,14,15；申18:15,18；撒下23:2；太11:9,10；彼後1:21）。擔任先知是上帝所選擇作祂自己和人類之間交流的媒介（見民12:6；摩3:7）。整部聖經就是藉著這個恩賜傳給人類的（見提後3:16；彼後1:20,21）。聖經為耶穌作見證的。稱先知恩賜是“為耶穌做見證”（啟19:10；見約5:39；啟12:17）的是很合適的。先知恩賜的運作方式的異象，異夢，以及上帝的特別啟示（見民12:6；啟1:1-3）。人類就這樣成為上帝的代言人（見撒下23:2；太3:3；彼後1:21）。上帝的旨意是要讓這個重要的屬靈恩賜伴隨著祂的教會直到末日（見珥2:28,29；啟12:17；19:10）。事實上，這將成為末時上帝真教會的一個標誌（啟12:17；19:10）。這樣解釋是非常合理的，因為自從亞當墮落以來，上帝一直藉著這個渠道向世人啟示祂自己並傳達祂的信息。
**辨別諸靈。**指辨別真假靈感的能力（見約壹4:1-3；《給傳道人的證言》第228,229頁）。基督警告祂的教會將有假先知興起，特別是在末期。所有的人都應當警醒識別並拒絕這種假教師（見太24:4,5,11,23-25）。早期教會的使徒有能力辨別基督教中的真假傳道人和教師（見徒5:1-10；13:9-11）。早期教會需要這種恩賜，因為當時無疑有許多人妄稱自己擁有這些恩賜。撒但隨時準備冒充真的恩賜，並往往藉著超自然的奇蹟來支持這些冒充者的虛假主張（帖後2:9；啟13:13,14）。
**說方言。**第14章詳細討論這種恩賜，與先知講道的恩賜進行對比。
**翻方言。**解釋所賜的信息需要特殊的恩賜（見14:27,28；14章附註）。

29.en: Are all apostles? The form of the question in Greek shows that a negative answer is expected. Verses 29, 30 show that God does not bestow any single gift to every believer. They are apportioned according to the need of the particular situation confronting the church at any place and time. It is also to be borne in mind that the gifts are not for the glorification and exaltation of man, but for the accomplishment of the plans and purposes of God, who imparts these powers to His people as He pleases, and not according to man’s ideas and opinions (see vs. 4, 5, 11). Not all believers at Corinth were qualified by the Holy Spirit to perform the duties of any one particular office in the church, such as that of teacher or prophet, but distribution of gifts was made by the Holy Spirit to such individuals as He chose to use for certain specific purposes. This should remove from the recipients of the gifts all pride and all ideas of superiority over their less favored brethren.
29.zh:
豈都是使徒嗎？豈都是先知嗎？豈都是教師嗎？豈都是行異能的嗎？

**豈都是使徒嗎。**原文問句的形式要求否定的的回答。29,30節說明上帝並沒有把任何一種恩賜給予每一個信徒。恩賜是在特定的時間和地點，根據教會所面臨的特殊需要而分配的。我們還要記住，恩賜不是為了榮耀或抬舉人，而是為了完成上帝的計劃和目的，上帝不是根據人的意見和看法，而是按照自己的旨意，將這些恩賜賜給祂子民的（見4,5,11節）。聖靈並沒有讓哥林多所有的信徒都在教會履行某一種特定的職責，例如作教師或先知。聖靈按照自己的揀選把恩賜給予這樣的人，來實行某種特殊的目的。所以領受恩賜的人不應有任何的驕傲，覺得自己比恩賜較少的弟兄優越。

4.en: Gifts. Gr. charismata, literally, “gifts of grace.” Here the word refers to the extraordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit dwelling and working in a special manner in individuals. The diversities of gifts are enumerated in vs. 8–11. Same Spirit. The different modes of operation of the gifts are all produced and controlled by the Holy Spirit. These various methods of working of the gifts are mentioned in vs. 8–11. Paul’s point of emphasis in referring to these different endowments is to show the Corinthians that since they are all produced by the same Spirit, and all have the same origin and purpose, therefore none are to be despised or belittled. No man, because of the reception of a certain gift of the Spirit, is to look with contempt upon any other believer because he is not so favored. The disposition of the gifts by God is to be accepted gratefully, and due recognition given to the One who dispenses these powers, and not to the recipient as being in any way superior to his fellows.
4.zh:
恩賜原有分別，聖靈卻是一位。

**恩賜。**charismata，指聖靈的特別恩賜以特殊的方式居住和運行在個人身上。8-11節列舉了各種聖靈的恩賜。
**聖靈卻是一位。**恩賜運行的不同方式都是由聖靈產生和控制的。8-11節提到這些恩賜運行的各種方式。保羅在提到這些不同的恩賜時向哥林多信徒強調，既然這些恩賜出於同一個聖靈，有著同一個來源和宗旨，就都不可予以輕視或小看。任何人都不可因領受聖靈的某種恩賜而輕看沒有這種恩賜的人。要以感恩的心領受上帝的恩賜，並承認那是分派這些恩賜的主所賜的，並不是因為領受的人比他的同胞有任何優越之處。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第314頁；《佈道論》第98頁；《證言》卷三第446頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–12節）**。《使徒行述》第92頁；《給傳道人的證言》第29頁；【 SDA6.1091】。

30.en: Gifts. This verse continues the argument of v. 29 (see comment there).
30.zh:
豈都是得恩賜醫病的嗎？豈都是說方言的嗎？豈都是翻方言的嗎？

**恩賜。**本節繼續29節的論述（見該節註釋）。

31.en: Coveth earnestly. Gr. zēloō, “to be zealous for.” The Corinthians are admonished to keep on earnestly beseeching the Lord to pour out His Spirit upon them and to impart to them gifts that are most necessary for the performance of their part in His work. The initial endowment with a gift or gifts is not necessarily the final endowment. As in the parable of the Talents (see on Matt. 25:14–30) faithfulness to duty may lead to increased endowments. Best. Gr. kreittona, “better,” though the comparative may stand for the superlative “best.” However, textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading “higher.” Spiritual gifts are imparted by the Holy Spirit for the building up of the church to a state of perfection and unity in Christ (see Eph. 4:12, 13). Doubtless those that deal directly with the main purpose of the church, namely, the preaching of the gospel, and that contribute most to the general edification (see 1 Cor. 14:1) are considered to be of primary importance. More excellent way. That is, the way of love described in ch. 13.
31.zh:
你們要切切的求那更大的恩賜。我現今把最妙的道指示你們。

**切切地求。**zēloo。保羅勸勉哥林多信徒人要熱切祈求上帝向他們傾降聖靈，把完成祂聖工所最需要的恩賜賜給他們。起初所賜予的恩賜並不等於最後所給予的。正如才幹的比喻（見太25:14-30註釋）那樣，忠於職責的僕人將獲得更多的恩賜。
**更大的。**kreittona，有文本為“更好的”，“最好的”。屬靈的恩賜是聖靈所賜的，為了建設教會在基督裡達到完美和統一（見弗4:12,13）。那些直接關係教會的主要目標，就是宣講福音，以及最有利於普及教育的恩賜（加林前14:1），無疑被認為是最重要的。
**最妙的道。**就是13章所描寫愛的方式。

28.en: God hath set. Literally, “God hath set for Himself.” In v. 11 the Holy Spirit is represented as dispensing the gifts; here it is God. The members of the Godhead work together in unity. Some. Paul means, some apostles, some prophets, etc. First. Doubtless first not only in point of time (see Matt. 10:1–8; DA 290, 291) but also in rank, as being one of the most important offices in the church. Apostles. Literally, “ones sent forth.” The term must not be limited to the Twelve. Others, too, were called apostles (see 1 Cor. 15:7; Gal. 1:19). The apostles seem to have had general jurisdiction over the churches. Prophets. See on v. 10. Teachers. Those endowed with special ability to expound the Scriptures. They are probably the same as those possessing the “word of knowledge,” who know how to unfold the mysteries of the kingdom of God to inquiring minds (v. 8). Preaching and teaching are closely allied; the preacher proclaims truth in a way that reaches the heart of the hearer and incites him to action in favor of what he has heard; the teacher takes truth and analyzes and synthesizes it with such clarity and logic that those who listen truly understand the message. They are thus enabled to give a reason for the hope that has been implanted in their hearts by the preacher. Miracles. The working of miracles was one of the more spectacular gifts of the Spirit. Miracles played a definite part in Christ’s ministry on earth, and He gave to His disciples the power to work miracles (see Matt. 10:8; DA 350, 351; EW 189). It was His plan that His followers should have power to perform miracles to advance His work on earth (see Mark 16:15–18; DA 823). See on 1 Cor. 12:10. Healings. See on v. 9. Helps. Gr. antilēpsis, derived from a verb meaning, literally, “to lay hold of.” The word occurs only here in the NT, but is frequent in the papyri, with the idea of “assistance,” “succor.” This gift is generally understood to be the ability conferred on those who perform the office of a deacon in the church, particularly as that office calls for ministering to the needs of the poor and the sick. This is a work that may not be given as much publicity as some of the other gifts, but it is nonetheless an important phase of church life. To be able to visit the sick and give them real sympathetic, understanding help, both physically and spiritually, is a powerful means of turning hearts to the Saviour. Caring for the poor and needy by relieving their material lack can be done satisfactorily only by those who are led by the Spirit. This is a most fruitful ministry (see Isa. 58:7; 5T 612, 613; 6T 282, 306, 307; MH 147, 148). Governments. Gr. kubernēseis, derived from a verb meaning “to steer,” “to act as a helmsman,” hence, “to guide,” “to govern.” Kubernēseis probably refers to the gifts of administration in the church. Tongues. For a definition of this gift see on ch. 14; see Additional Note on Chapter 14.
28.zh:
神在教會所設立的：第一是使徒，第二是先知，第三是教師，其次是行異能的，再次是得恩賜醫病的，幫助人的，治理事的，說方言的。

**上帝在教會所設立的。**直譯為“上帝所親自設立的”。11節說聖靈分配恩賜；這裡說是上帝。三位一體的上帝是共同工作的。
**第一。**無疑不僅從時間上說（見太10:1-8；《歷代願望》290，291頁），也是從等級上說，指教會中最重要的職分之一。
**使徒。**直譯為“奉差遣的人”，不限於十二使徒，也有其他的人被稱為使徒的（見林前15:7；加1:19）。使徒似乎對眾教會擁有總的管轄權。
**先知。**見第10節註釋。
**教師。**指那些被賦予特別能力講解聖經的人。他們可能就是那些擁有“知識的言語”的人，知道怎樣向渴慕的人（第8節）講解上帝之國的奧秘。講道和教導有密切的聯繫；傳道人宣講真理，打動聽眾的心，激發他們對所聽見的話作出反應。教師則以清晰而符合邏輯的方法分析和綜合真理，使聽眾能真正明白真理的信息。他們就這樣為傳道人播撒在聽眾心中的盼望提供理由。
**行異能的。**行異能是聖靈顯著的恩賜之一。基督在地上傳道時，行神蹟佔了一定的比例，祂賜給祂的門徒行異能的能力（見太10:8；《歷代願望》350，351頁；《早期著作》189頁）。祂的計劃是讓祂的門徒擁有行異能的能力，以推進祂在地上的工作（見可16:15-18；《歷代願望》823頁）。見林前12:10註釋。
**醫病的。**見第9節註釋。
**幫助人的。**antilēpsis，源於一個意為“控制”的動詞。該詞在《新約》中只出現這一次，但在紙莎草文獻中多次出現，有“幫助”之意。這個恩賜通常被理解為在教會中擔任執事的能力，特別是幫助窮苦患病之人的需要。這項工作不像其他恩賜那樣顯眼，但卻是教會生活的一個重要方面。探訪病人，真正地同情理解他們，在肉體和屬靈上幫助他們，這是引人歸向救主的有力手段。關照貧乏的人，減輕他們的經濟負擔，這樣的工作只有聖靈所引導的人才能勝任。這是一項最有成效的傳道工作（見賽58:7；《教會證言》卷五612,613頁；《教會證言》卷六282,306,307頁；《服務真詮》147，148頁）。
**治理事的。**kubernēseis，源於一個意為“操駛”的動詞，故有“引導”，“管理”之意。Kubernēseis可能指教會中管理的恩賜。
**說方言的。**關於這個恩賜，見林前14章註釋；林前14章補充註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第92頁；《證言》卷三第446頁。

1.zh:
弟兄們，論到屬靈的恩賜，我不願意你們不明白。

**論到。**本章開始了一個新的主題，延續到第14章最後，那就是屬靈的恩賜。人們對於這個題目無疑有很多的誤解。擁有不同恩賜的人之間也存在不幸的爭端，並且顯然還有濫用恩賜的的現象。
**屬靈的恩賜。**“恩賜”一詞是外加的，但依據上下文顯然是需要的。這些恩賜是耶穌昇天以後以特殊的方式賜給教會的（弗4:8,11），其目的是為了使教會合而為一，以合適的狀態迎接主（見弗4:12-15）。哥林多信徒顯然詢問保羅聖靈的恩賜中哪一個比較大的問題。他們中有些人自誇所擁有的恩賜比其他信徒更大更重要（見林前12:18-23）。保羅利用他們提出的問題，教導他們聖靈在基督奧秘的身體，就是祂的教會中運行的題目。上帝的聖靈從一開始就在教會中運行（見《使徒行述》37，53頁；《先祖與先知》593，594頁；《天路》218頁）。所以聖靈的恩賜並不限於新約時代。古時許多先知的存在證明了這一點。上帝的旨意和計劃是要讓祂的教會獲得聖靈的恩賜直到末日（弗4:8,11-13；《使徒行述》54，55頁）。這些恩賜都是從上帝那裡來的。所以人根本沒有理由在同胞面前因蒙上天揀選為彰顯祂能力的工具，以特殊的方式幫助整個教會而自誇（見林前12:11）。
請注意聖靈恩賜與聖靈果子區別（加5:22,23）。聖靈的恩賜是上帝的能力賜給教會中的個人，為成就祂完善祂教會的目的。聖靈的果子是教會中那些全然讓降伏自己接受聖靈的引導，並被聖靈的最高品質，就是愛所激勵的信徒表現出來的品格（林前13:13；加5:22,23；《使徒行述》388頁；《天路》68，69頁；《教會證言》卷五169頁；《教會證言》卷四355頁）。
**不明白。**保羅迫切希望哥林多人不要誤解聖靈恩賜的真正性質，以及這些恩賜在教會中的正確使用。澄清這個問題，無疑是因為哥林多信徒剛剛擺脫了異教（見第2節）。在信奉異教的時候，他們不瞭解真神的啟示和聖靈的感化。因此未能對這些新的經驗形成正確的觀點，除非他們受到小心的教誨，並毫無保留地接受這種教導。原先影響他們的勢力在他們接受救主時就摧毀了。上帝的能力藉著聖靈的恩賜特地堅固了他們。

2.zh:
你們作外邦人的時候，隨事被牽引，受迷惑，去服事那啞巴偶像，這是你們知道的。

**外邦人。**ethne。指猶太人以外的所有人，但在基督徒心目中也有“異教徒”之意。本節似乎就是這個意思。保羅說哥林多信徒曾經是異教徒，敬拜偶像，不認識真神，迷信假神。引誘他們進入歧途的勢力乃是黑暗的權勢，是他們所敬拜的假神所代表的邪靈（見10:20）。他們如果認識到接受基督教所帶來的好處，就會為自己身為基督徒的現狀而感恩。保羅在其他地方也提到他們原為異教徒的景況，以鼓勵基督徒感謝上帝藉著福音向他們所顯的憐憫（見羅6:17；弗2:11,12；多3:3）。
**受誘惑。**表明他們不能自制，被一種身外的勢力拉到偶像崇拜之中，無法抗拒。這種勢力無疑利用他們的情感和食慾迷惑他們，使他們相信崇拜偶像有好處，而事實上他們卻因而毀滅。
**啞巴。**他們被引誘到偶像的祭壇和廟宇崇拜，獻祭或求問。但這些偶像與永生的上帝相比，乃是無聲的的“啞巴”。上帝則在聖經中顯示祂自己，賜給祂子民屬靈的恩賜，使他們能奉祂的名說話。上帝常常用異教假神的啞口無聲的來論證崇拜假神的愚昧（詩115:4,5；135:15-17；哈2:18,19）。因此任何超自然的表現或聲音，都是來自魔鬼的勢力，而不是來自偶像或偶像所代表的假神。

3.zh:
所以我告訴你們，被神的靈感動的，沒有說耶穌是可咒詛的；若不是被聖靈感動的，也沒有能說耶穌是主的。

**所以。**為了使他們正確地認識聖靈在人心中的工作，特別是據說來自這個源頭的話語，保羅為他們提供了一條辨別真偽的準則。
**可咒詛。**anathema，“該滅亡的”（見羅9:3註釋）。這裡提供了一條簡單的原則，使我們知道一個自稱受聖靈感動的人是否真是受上帝引導的。被聖靈感動的人不會說基督是被咒詛的或該滅亡的。任何被聖靈感動的人都不會貶損耶穌，更不可能說祂是被咒詛該滅亡的人了。這種話語足以證明說的人無論他自稱是什麼，肯定不是受聖靈感動的。上帝的靈在任何情況下都是榮耀基督的，並促使一切受祂感動的人敬愛並尊重基督的名（見約壹4:1-3）。
**耶穌是主。**凡不受上帝的靈感動的人不會承認耶穌是上帝的聖子。然而沒有受聖靈感動的人也可能在口頭上承認基督為主或救主，不過那是惡人的偽裝。真心承認耶穌為主，只能出自被聖靈引導之人的口（參太16:16,17）。凡真正榮耀耶穌之名和祂聖工的人會證明自己是受聖靈感動的。人若不受聖靈引導，認識救主的神性，就不會真正愛基督，以及祂的聖名和聖工。凡隨從自己未悔改之心的慾望和情感的人，是不可能表現出熱愛耶穌聖名和聖工的。不論何人接受基督，都是藉著上帝的靈。反之，人若藐視耶穌，以任何方式侮辱祂的聖工，教導與祂的道相反的道理，就表明他不是受聖靈引導的（見《歷代願望》412頁）。應當祈求並珍惜聖靈的臨格。拒絕聖靈、使祂憂傷離去，就是從內心排除對救主的一切真正認識，會導致冷淡，黑暗，和最後屬靈的死亡（見弗4:30；《歷代願望》587，588頁）。

14.zh:
身子原不是一個肢體，乃是許多肢體。

**身子。**保羅在14-26節中指出，組織的團結乃是包容而不是排除大多數成員。他用人體組織來說明這個道理。人體的各個肢體都各司其責。身體若要不斷地發揮功能，沒有一個部分是可以放棄的。這裡形象地提出不同的肢體來說明這個問題。
**一個肢體。**人體由不同的肢體構成。它們執行多種功能。教會中也存在類似的差異。不要指望大家都一樣，或認為上帝安排在教會里的肢體有哪一個是無用的。人體不只需要多樣的肢體，教會不只是需要多種的人。它們都應為整體的利益而在肢體之間合作互補，履行所有必要的功能。人體不需要，也沒有地方安置懶惰而對整體不作出有效貢獻的肢體。同樣，教會也需要獻身積極的肢體在工作中不斷作出貢獻，爭取人進入上帝的國（見《教會證言》卷四590頁；《教會證言》卷五456,457頁；《教會證言》卷六434,435頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–21節）**。《證言》卷四第128頁；《證言》卷五第279頁；《證言》卷六第288頁；《論福利工作》第123頁。

15.zh:
設若腳說：我不是手，所以不屬乎身子；他不能因此就不屬乎身子。

**不屬乎身子。**沒有一個肢體有理由說，因為它不在身體事務中起較大的作用，它就是不需要的，不是身體必需的部分。同樣，沒有哪一個基督奧秘身體的肢體可以說，因為他不擔任某一職位，他就是無用的，與教會關係不大。教會中最卑微的成員和恩賜最大的成員一樣，都是基督的肢體（見太23:8-12；雅3:1；彼前5:3）。每一個肢體都是基督所疼愛的。祂為所有的人捨命。祂願意為一個人受死（見路15:4-7；《歷代願望》480頁；《教會證言》卷八73頁）。

16.zh:
設若耳說：我不是眼，所以不屬乎身子；他也不能因此就不屬乎身子。

**耳。**這裡的論據15節相同（見15節註釋）。

17.zh:
若全身是眼，從哪裡聽聲呢？若全身是耳，從哪裡聞味呢？

**眼。**如果教會所有的肢體都有一樣的恩賜，大家都從事同樣的工作或服務，那就疏忽了教會傳福音活動中的一些重要方面，教會在屬靈和能力方面就會衰落。每一個肢體都要為身體的利益作出應有的貢獻，否則就不能保持最大的效能。
**聞味。**要充分享受生活，身體沒有一個感官是可以取消的。有人可能認為嗅覺不如聽覺和視覺重要，但稍加思考就能明白，一個缺乏嗅覺的人要遭遇別人可以避免的許多危險。因為別人通過嗅覺神經能夠辨別危險的物質。上帝不會做任何對教會沒有益處的事晴。他對於教會的計劃是好的，而不是壞的（見耶29:11；弗5:27）。上帝為教會的成長和建設所提供的各樣屬靈恩賜都有其重要作用，取消了任何一樣都會遭致損失。每一個肢體都要知道自己對主的虧欠，並完全順服祂的旨意，愉快地接受上帝安排他服侍教會的任何位置。

18.zh:
但如今，神隨自己的意思把肢體俱各安排在身上了。

**上帝隨自己。**上帝本著祂的智慧給身體的不同肢體安排了不同的功能。人無法左右這種安排；它完全出於上帝。同樣，祂為哥林多的各位信徒指派了不同的工作。每一個人蒙揀選都是本著上帝的智慧，並獲得一種恩賜來負起所託付他的責任（見27,28節）。恩賜是上帝所分配的，人不能參與（見第11節註釋）。一個肢體如果埋怨拒絕他在教會中的位置和工作，他就是背叛上帝。

19.zh:
若都是一個肢體，身子在哪裡呢？

**一個肢體。**哥林多顯然有人對上帝所分配的恩賜抱著不滿的精神。那些沒有在教會中擔任重要職位的人似乎不高興，覺得自己如果不作傳道人或教師就無足輕重了。保羅設法消除這種錯誤的思想。他指出，如果人體的所有部位都擔任某一個肢體，如眼或耳，那將是多麼荒謬
**身子。**手，腳，眼，耳等要履行分配給他們的工作，就必須連在身體上；如果這種聯合破壞了，就沒有一個肢體能發揮它的功能。如果全身的力量都集中到某一個肢體，如眼睛上，所有其他的肢體就會蒙受損失，而眼睛本身失去了用途。保羅就這樣強調，任何干預創造主為人體正常功能所作安排的行為，其結果都是有害無益的。

20.zh:
但如今肢體是多的，身子卻是一個。

**但如今。**樂意接受上帝對於受造者和祂教會的計劃，就有平安與喜樂。
**身子卻是一個。**在差異中有統一，在統一中有差異，這種安排能產生最好的效果（見結1:28；10；《教會證言》卷五751頁；《傳道良助》489頁）。上帝的聖手掌管一切。每一位基督徒都可以因被視為有價值的一分子而喜樂，即便他在光榮完成救贖計劃的大工中擔任最小的工作。

21.zh:
眼不能對手說：我用不著你；頭也不能對腳說：我用不著你。

**用不著。**本節責備了那些自以為天賦甚高之人的驕傲，說明他們看法是錯誤的。他們的驕傲是他們認為用不著恩賜較少的人。教會生活的不同部門要相互依賴，才能正常發揮整體的功能。恩賜多的肢體和恩賜少的肢體同樣需要相互依靠。既是這樣，教會中就完全沒有驕傲或不滿的餘地。身體的每一部分都有其獨特的功能，一個部分失效就會影響所有其他部分的效能。因此教會中那表面上似乎最不重要的職能，對於整個組織的有效運作與和諧發展卻是至關重要的。
弟兄們不可驕傲與不滿，而當彼此表顯愛心與憐憫。那些看似恩賜較多的人應當珍惜恩賜較少的弟兄，讓他們知道自己欣賞他們為全體教會信徒熱愛的事業所作的貢獻（見《教會證言》卷五279頁）。所有的信徒都當記住基督徒中間所表顯的愛和團結，乃是上帝自己所指定的方法，以告訴世人祂差遣了祂的兒子來到這個世界（見約17:21）。

22.zh:
不但如此，身上肢體人以為軟弱的，更是不可少的。

**以為軟弱。**不知道保羅所指的是身上的哪些肢體。也許是指身體中比較軟弱，需要保護的部位。
**不可少的。**一個人如果失去了一隻手、一條腿、一隻眼睛或一隻耳朵，他也許能繼續存活下去。但如果他沒有了心臟，肺或大腦，他就不能存活。這些器官雖然看上去比較軟弱，需要保護，但事實上他們更加重要，因而比堅固的部分如手臂和腿更加有用。

23.zh:
身上肢體，我們看為不體面的，越發給他加上體面；不俊美的，越發得著俊美。

**不體面的。**保羅並沒有另眼看待這些肢體。它們無疑也是正常著裝的。這些肢體與“不俊美的”肢體之間的區別似乎只是程度而已。後者可能指性器官或排洩器官。人們習慣把臉部露出來，不加任何遮掩，手也是這樣。但身體的某些部位，按照謙卑，端莊和合宜的要求應該遮掩起來。這種遮蔽身體某些部分的做法起源於人類墮落的記載。罪惡進入人間之前，我們的始祖是以榮光遮體的。但是罪惡使榮光消退。亞當和夏娃既看見了自己裸體，就試圖把自己遮掩起來（見創2:25；3:7,10,11；《先祖與先知》45，57頁）。上帝希望祂的子民充分地把自己遮蔽起來，以保證滿足基督徒謙卑和純潔的要求。
**加上體面。**沒有遮蔽的臉部，自然被認為是體面的。身體的其他部位則應體面地遮掩起來。這似乎是教導說，教會中那些屬靈恩賜比別人少的人，不應受到輕視或冷遇，而要更加關心和愛護他們，因為他們對於整個身體是不可缺少的。

24.zh:
我們俊美的肢體，自然用不著裝飾；但神配搭這身子，把加倍的體面給那有缺欠的肢體，

**用不著裝飾。**這句話與23節結合在一起則更為自然。臉，手等部位不需要遮蔽，暴露出來不會導致尷尬或恥辱。同樣，教會中恩賜較多的肢體不必得到恩賜較少的肢體所需要的引導和屬靈教訓。
**配搭。**sugkerannumi，直譯為“混合”。該詞只出現在這裡與來4:2中，在本節可能指按照次序組合起來。有文本為“調整”。上帝使一個肢體與另一個肢體相互依靠，併為其他肢體的合宜行動所必需。所有的肢體都在一個和諧的整體裡一起工作。
**加倍的體面。**得到更多的關心和照顧。一個人必須工作，生產，才能獲得所需要的衣服，來遮蔽這些肢體。
**懷愛倫註釋（24–27節）**。《使徒行述》第318頁。

25.zh:
免得身上分門別類，總要肢體彼此相顧。

**分門別類。**schisma（見林前1:10註釋）。教會各肢體的不同才幹與恩賜，不應成為分門結黨的理由。不要讓任何人覺得他與那群被認為恩賜較多的人是格格不入的。這裡似乎是指哥林多教會里所發生的結黨紛爭（見1:10-12；11:18）。身體的所有肢體都是需要的，而且相互依賴。沒有一個肢體可以被認為是全身的利益所不需要的。教會也是這樣。任何教會的成員，不論多麼軟弱，沒有學識，默默無聞，都不能被認為是不必要或無價值的。每一個人的崗位都是需要的，不可認為他們是屬於不同的團體而不能交往。
**相顧。**無論身體的哪一個部位疼痛或患病，全身的資源和精力都要集中起來解除疼痛，使受到傷害的肢體恢復正常。同樣，在屬靈的身體中，每一個肢體也要關心促進他同道的利益，而不管他是什麼人，或有什麼恩賜。

27.zh:
你們就是基督的身子，並且各自作肢體。

**你們。**原文的代詞是強調的。保羅寫信給哥林多信徒。他們當中有人在教會里分門結黨，有人還沒有斷絕與偶像的關係，還有人道德敗壞（見1:10,11；3:3；5:1,2；8:1）。他們應當謹慎，作完美健康的肢體，在教會的工作中儘自己的本分。他們應當忠於基督並彼此忠誠，不要嫉妒任何其他兄弟。
**基督的身子。**參弗1:22,23；4:4,12,16；5:23,30；西1:18,24；2:19；3:15。教會的肢體應當在凡事上順服基督的旨意，就像身體的各肢體順從大腦的意志那樣。身體的所有肢體與大腦之間，以及彼此之間都應保持活潑的聯繫，基督徒也當與同一身體的其他肢體保持聯絡，大家都順服同一個頭，就是基督。
**各自做肢體。**ek merous。每一個肢體都有責任在自己的崗位上發揮各自的功能來侍奉上帝。28-31節進一步闡述了這一點，說明教會信徒的不同功能乃是出於聖靈的不同恩賜。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五第731頁；《證言》卷七第296頁；《證言》卷八第174頁；見來8：1，2懷愛倫註釋。

11.en: Child. Gr. nēpios, literally, a “non-speaker,” an “infant.” Here the apostle uses the illustration of the differences between the experiences of childhood and those of manhood to emphasize the great difference that exists between the dim understanding of things possessed by men now, and the bright light of knowledge that will be theirs in heaven. Spake. Or, “used to speak,” that is, it was my habit to speak. The meaningless sounds made by a child who is learning to talk are here compared with the wisdom that will replace earthly knowledge in the future, immortal state. When one reaches manhood he lays aside as of no value the ideas and feelings of childhood, which formerly seemed of such great importance. In a similar way, when heaven is reached, men will lay aside the ideas, views, and feelings that are cherished in this life and are considered so valuable and important. Understood. Or, “used to think,” that is, it was my habit to think. This refers to the early, undeveloped exercise of the childish mind, a mode of thought that cannot be regarded as connected reasoning. The understanding was narrow and imperfect, and knowledge was meager. Things that occupied the attention then, lost their value as adulthood was reached. Thought. Or, “used to reason,” that is, it was my habit to reason. The thinking and reasoning of childhood appear puerile, shortsighted, inconclusive, and erroneous to an adult. So it will be when God’s people are in the kingdom of glory; there will be as much difference between earthly plans, opinions, understanding, and reasoning powers and those of heaven as there is between those of childhood and those of manhood. Put away. Gr. katargeō (see on v. 8).
11.zh:
我作孩子的時候，話語像孩子，心思像孩子，意念像孩子，既成了人，就把孩子的事丟棄了。

**孩子。**nēpios，直譯為“不會說話的人”，“嬰兒”。使徒在本節用兒童和成年人狀態的差異，來強調人類現有淺薄的知識與他們將來到天上所擁有輝煌的知識亮光之間的區別。
**話語。**或“說話方式”，即這是我說話的習慣。本節用兒童學說話時無意義的發聲與將來在永生中替代屬世知識的智慧相比較。一個人長大成人以後，就會拋棄兒童時代所看重的思想感情。同樣，當人類來到天上時，就會拋棄今生所極為看重的觀點，想法和情感。
**心思。**或“思維方式”，即這是我思維的習慣。兒童未發育的思維方式，不能被認為具有連貫性。他的見解狹隘而片面，知識也貧乏。他們心中所想的，長大以後就失去了價值。
**意念。**或“推理方式”，即我推理的習慣。在一個成年人看來，兒童的思維和推理方式是幼稚，目光短淺，不確定而錯誤的。同樣，當上帝的子民來到榮耀的國度時，就會發現地上的計劃，觀點，認識和推理能力都與天上有很大的區別，正如兒童與成人的區別一樣。
**丟棄。**katargeo（見第8節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第119，213頁；《證言》卷三第194頁。

10.en: Perfect. Gr. teleios, “complete,” “entire,” “fully mature.” Even the knowledge acquired by the most brilliant of men is insignificant when compared with the vast ocean of knowledge in the universe. Thus the boasting of the Corinthians was completely out of place (see ch. 8:1, 2). When Jesus Christ comes again to redeem His own, then the partial illumination of the human mind by all the knowledge possessed by man will be lost to view in the superior brightness of the divine revelation of truth, even as the light from the stars disappears when the morning sun appears. Shall be done away. Gr. katargeō (see on v. 8). There can be no suggestion here that knowledge of truth will ever cease or pass away; truth is eternal, and the knowledge that man has of eternal truth will always remain. It is the partial nature of that knowledge that will cease when man is changed form mortal to immortal (see v. 12; cf. ch. 8:2). Likewise, when this world comes to an end, and men hold open, face-to-face communion with God, prophecy will have served its purpose and will no longer be needed.
10.zh:
等那完全的來到，這有限的必歸於無有了。

**完全的。**teleios，或“完全成熟的”。即使是最聰明的人所擁有的知識，在宇宙知識的大海洋中，也會顯得毫無意義。所以哥林多信徒的誇口是完全不合時宜的（見8:1,2）。當耶穌基督再來救贖自己的子民時，人類知識的微光就會消失在上帝真理啟示的無比輝煌之中，就像星光在晨曦出現時黯然失色一樣。
**必歸於無有。**katargeo（見第8節註釋）。這裡並沒有暗示真理的知識會止息或過時。真理是永恆的；人類永恆真理的知識將永垂不朽。當人從必死的狀態變成不朽的時候，他們所擁有的，將不再是淺薄的知識（見12節；參8:2）。同樣，當這個世界結束時，人類將面對面與上帝交通。先知講道既完成了自己的使命，就不再需要了。

7.en: Beareth. Gr. stegō, “to cover closely,” “to protect by covering”; “to sustain,” “to support.” Love conceals and is silent about such things as the faults of others, which the selfishness of the natural heart would gladly expose. Love is not desirous of inspecting the weaknesses of others or of allowing them to be inspected by anyone else. Believeth all things. This phrase does not mean that one who loves his fellow men is credulous to the point of absurdity, making no distinction between the things to be believed, and thus as likely to believe a falsehood as the truth. But love is disposed to put the best possible construction on the conduct of others, imputing good motives to them. This is the attitude of love, because love seeks to make others happy and will not believe anything to their detriment except on irrefutable evidence. In relation to God, love believes without question everything that is revealed of the will of God for man. There is no doubt concerning God’s Word and His instructions; all is gratefully accepted and obeyed. Hopeth. However dark appearances may be, and whatever grounds there may be for questioning the sincerity of others, love still hopes that everything will be well in the end, and will maintain this position until all possibility of its being confirmed has disappeared. This faith in one’s neighbor, which love inspires, leads to the championing of his cause in the face of opposition. Love is based upon trust, and this trust rests ultimately in God; therefore love is willing to face ridicule, strife, and contempt in defense of others, hoping that in due time truth will be vindicated. Endureth. Love suffers quietly all the difficulties, trials, persecutions, and injuries inflicted by man, and all the attacks that God may see fit to allow the adversary to make (see Job 13:15). This statement about love shows the infinite patience that is possessed by him who is always is always under the control of love. The strange behavior of others, perhaps calculated to hurt or annoy him, he patiently bears, for he sees in his fellow men souls for whom Christ died, souls that are misled by Satan, and therefore to be pitied and helped rather than condemned or treated harshly. Being the perfect exposition of the law of God, love consistently works for the best interests of others, and consequently is prepared to look upon the unfavorable conduct of others with an understanding patience and sympathy inspired by God (see Matt. 22:37–40; Rom. 13:10; 1 John 4:7, 12, 16, 18, 20, 21).
7.zh:
凡事包容，凡事相信，凡事盼望，凡事忍耐。

**包容。**stego，“緊緊遮蓋”，“遮掩保護”，“維持”，“支持”。愛心遮掩別人的過錯並保持沉默。只有自私之心的本性才喜歡暴露別人的過錯。愛心不願意查究別人的軟弱，也不讓任何其他人來查究。
**凡事相信。**這並不是說人愛同胞可以輕信到荒謬的地步，不問青紅皂白，全都相信，連虛謊也當作真理來相信。但愛心總是用最好的動機來解釋別人的行為。這就是愛的態度，因為愛會努力使別人快樂，不相信任何有害於別人的事情，除非有確鑿的證據。在與上帝的關係中，愛心毫無疑問地相信上帝的旨意向人所啟示的一切真理。不懷疑上帝的道和教訓；懷著感恩的心領受和順從這一切。
**盼望。**不論在表面上看有多麼黑暗，不論有什麼理由懷疑別人的真誠，愛總心是盼望最終有好結果，並堅持這種看法直到所有的理由全都消失。這種愛所激勵的對同胞的信心，會使他冒著反對維護自己的事業。愛是以信任為基礎的。這種信心最終的對象乃是上帝；所以愛就是樂意冒著嘲笑，紛爭和藐視保護別人，並盼望到時候真理會得到高舉。
**忍耐。**愛心會默默忍受人為的一切困難、試煉、逼迫和傷害，以及上帝許可下的仇敵攻擊（見伯13:15）。這句關於愛的話語表明在愛心控制下的人擁有無限的忍耐。別人的反常行為，原本是要傷害或惹怒他的，都被他忍受了，因為他在同胞身上看到的，是基督所為之死，而又被撒但所誤導的靈魂，應該得到同情和幫助，而不是譴責和攻擊。愛完全表達了上帝的律法，不斷為別人的最高利益而努力，其結果就是以上帝所激發的體諒和同情看待他人不友善的舉動（見太22:37-40；羅13:10；約壹4:7,12,16,18,20,21）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第498頁；《證言》卷二第135頁；《證言》卷四第27頁；《證言》卷五第404頁。

13.en: Abideth. This word conveys the idea of permanence. Exclusive of love, all the things that have been dealt with in this chapter, including prophecy, tongues, and other gifts of the Spirit, will cease to be of value or will be canceled, but the three basic elements of Christian experience will not pass away; they are permanent. Therefore the Christian is exhorted to concentrate his attention on these. Faith, here not the spiritual gift known as faith (see on ch. 12:9) but the experience described in Heb. 11 (cf. on Rom. 4:3), must be of eternal value, for it will ever be an essential of harmonious life in the new earth. Hope, being a desire for an object and an expectation of obtaining it, will by its very nature be a part of the experience in heaven, where there will ever be fresh fields for the people of God to explore and new delights for them to enjoy (see 1 Cor. 2:9; Ed 306, 307). All the treasures of heaven cannot be enjoyed at once by the redeemed, and as long as there is anything that is to be desired and expected for the future, hope will exist. Greatest. When it is realized that of all qualities of character, love is the one that inspiration uses to describe the very nature of God, it is easy to see why the apostle should say that above all gifts of the Spirit, this is the greatest (see 1 John 4:7, 8, 16). As a manner of life, love is more effective, more victorious, more satisfying, than the possession and exercise of the various gifts of the Spirit enumerated in ch. 12 (see 1 Cor. 12:31). Love for God and our fellow men is the highest expression of harmony with God (see Matt. 22:37–40; 8T 139). Love lived out in the life of the believer is the great test of the sincerity of one’s Christianity (see Isa. 58:6–8; Matt. 25:34–40; 6T 273–280). To be a Christian is to be like Christ, who “went about doing good” (Acts 10:38). Christians, then, are those who, in the spirit of Jesus, go about doing good to all who need their help. They do it with no self-interest, but because the love of God in their hearts makes it impossible for them to do anything else (see 6T 268; 3T 524). Love is the superexcellent way, because its practical expression is the test that is to decide the eternal destiny of all men. Those whose religion is one of mere outward compliance with forms and observances will discover that such is not acceptable to God (see 5T 612). Self- denying love, producing unity among the believers, will convince the world that God did send His Son into the world to save mankind. This is God’s chosen method for His people to bear testimony to the truth of the gospel (see John 17:21, 23). Such love, which shows no desire to exalt, justify, or gratify self, but is dedicated to selfless ministry to the needy, is an argument that unconverted men cannot gainsay. They see in it something incomprehensible to their philosophy of life. Their hearts are touched, and their intelligence responds to the evidence of the power of godliness in the lives of converted men. Thus love is demonstrated to be the greatest way of preaching the gospel and advancing the kingdom of God.
13.zh:
如今常存的有信，有望，有愛這三樣，其中最大的是愛。

**常存的。**該詞有永恆的意思。除了愛之外，本章所講到的一切，包括先知講道，方言和其他聖靈的恩賜，都將失去價值或取消，但基督徒經驗的三個基本要素將不會過時，因為它們是永恆的。所以使徒勸勉基督徒要關注這些事情。
這裡的信不是指信心的屬靈恩賜（見林前12:9註釋），而是指《希伯來書》11章所描寫的經驗（參羅4:3註釋）。它具有永恆的價值，是新天新地和諧生活的要素。望，就是盼望得到某樣東西，其性質是天國經驗的一部分，那裡不斷有新的領域供上帝的子民探索，有新的喜樂供他們享受（見林前2:9；《教育論》306，307頁）。贖民不可能馬上享受天國的全部財富。只要對將來有所企望，就會有盼望存在。
**最大的。**如果我們認識到在所有的品質中，愛是聖靈用來描述上帝本性的，我們就不難看出為什麼使徒說愛在一切聖靈的恩賜中是最大的（見約壹4:7,8,16）。愛作為一種生活方式，比擁有和運用12章所例舉的各樣聖靈恩賜（見林前12:31）更加有效，更有勝利的能力，更加令人滿足。愛上帝愛同胞是與上帝和諧的最高表現（見太22:37-40；《教會證言》卷八第139頁）。信徒生活中所表現的愛是基督教信仰真實性的偉大明證（見賽58:6-8；太25:34-40；《教會證言》卷六第273-280頁）。
作一個基督徒就要像基督。祂曾“周流四方行善事”（徒10:38）。當時的基督徒是那些本著耶穌的精神周流四方為需要他們幫助的人行善的人。他們不求自己的益處，但因為上帝的愛在他們心中，使他們不可能做別的事情（見《教會證言》卷六第268頁；《教會證言》卷三第524頁）。愛是最高的品質，因為愛的實際表現將決定所有人的永久命運。如果人的信仰只是在外表上遵守儀式和禮節，他們將發現這樣作是不能蒙上帝悅納的（見《教會證言》卷五第612頁）。克己的愛會在信徒中間造成團結，使世人相信上帝確實差遣祂的兒子到世上來拯救人類。這是上帝為祂的子民所選擇的方法，好為福音的真理做見證（見約17:21,23）。這樣的愛沒有抬舉，維護或滿足自己的願望，一心一意無私地為需要的人服務，乃是未悔改的人所不能否認的證據。他們從中看到一些他們的人生觀所無法理解的東西。他們的心被感動了。於是他們的理智就回應悔改之人生活中虔誠能力的見證。愛就是這樣證明為傳揚福音、推進上帝國度最偉大的方式。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第319頁；《醫療佈道論》第251頁；《證言》卷三第187頁；《論福利工作》第32頁。

5.en: Behave itself unseemly. Gr. aschēmoneo, “to act unbecomingly,” “to behave dishonorably.” In the LXX the word is used with the meaning, “to be naked” (see Eze. 16:7, 22; etc.). Love is never uncivil, rude, or unmannerly; it never behaves in such a way as to offend the sensibilities of others. Christ, when on earth, was ever mindful of the feelings of men, and He ever acted with courtesy and propriety toward all (see GW 121). Every true follower of the Lord will be courteous at all times, never responding to the promptings of the natural heart to repay rudeness and harshness with discourtesy (see GW 123). Love always searches for that which is right and proper or becoming in all the relations of life, because it seeks to promote the happiness of others, and that of necessity leads to avoidance of everything that would cause offense or interfere with true enjoyment. There may be an allusion here to the improper conduct of some of the Corinthians in public worship and in relation to heathen feasts (see 1 Cor. 8:10–12; 11:4–6, 20–22). For the Christian, personal opinions, desires, and practices are supplanted by love in the interests of the comfort, convenience, and happiness of others. The becoming behavior of love precludes all fanaticism and unbalanced positions that lead to unrestrained emotional outbursts and bring the cause of God into disrepute. This statement that love never behaves unseemly proves that it is under the control of reason at all times, and cannot be mere emotion or feeling. That which is simply a response to feeling and emotion, and falsely called love, does not act reasonably, nor does it necessarily consider the feelings and sensibilities of others. Her own. Literally, “her own [things].” The exact opposite of the nature of real love is a selfish seeking after one’s own advantage, influence or honor as the great objective in life (see ch. 10:24, 33). Of all the characteristics of love, this is the hardest for the unsanctified heart to understand. Man naturally is interested first of all in himself, and frequently that interest overshadows all others; but Christ’s way, the way of love, puts self last and others first (see on Matt. 5:43–46; 7:12). Man’s selfish nature is one more proof that sin has completely reversed the divine order in the experience of humanity, leading men to concentrate their affections and interests on themselves (see Jer. 17:9; Rom. 7:14–18, 20; 8:5–8; James 4:4; see on Matt. 10:39). One possessed of the selfless love of God forgets self and is completely absorbed in doing the will of God. That is why he is willing to give his life in loving ministry for others (see Matt. 22:37–39; Acts 10:38; GW 112; 7T 9, 10). Jesus “went about doing good” (Acts 10:38). From this statement it is clear that no one can be a real Christian, a real follower of Christ, who lives for himself alone or who makes it his principal object in life to promote his own interests. A Christian is one who follows Christ. Therefore he is one who denies the clamors of the natural heart for devotion to self, and who is willing to sacrifice his own comfort, time, ease, wealth, and talents to advance the welfare of mankind. Easily provoked. The word “easily” is supplied, and apparently without warrant. It actually gives a wrong shade of meaning to the statement. Love is not provoked, whether easily or otherwise; nothing can disturb the equanimity of perfect love and cause a display of annoyance, impatience, or anger. To insert the word “easily” would be to suggest that there are times when a certain amount of anger, irritability, or resentment are permissible, but such is not the case with real love (see Ps. 119:165; Heb. 12:3; 1 Peter 2:23). The Christian who knows that self, the natural heart, is opposed to the will of God, and that having committed himself to the Lord, he is dead to sin, has no cause for irritation or annoyance. He simply turns everything over to God, knowing that whatever happens, he is under the watchful, loving eye of One who is controlling all things for his good (see Rom. 6:11; 8:28; 1 Peter 5:6, 7). One of the most striking effects of conversion is the remarkable change that is seen naturally the character of a person who was naturally irritable in disposition, resentful, and readily roused to anger. Under the influence of the Holy Spirit such a one becomes mild, gentle, and calm. All efforts of Satan to annoy him and make him give way to the old quick-tempered spirit are unavailing. Thinketh no evil. Literally, “does not reckon the evil.” The Greek here conveys the idea of not taking into account the wrong that has been done; not reckoning, imputing, or charging the wrong to any man’s account. This is another beautiful, Christlike attribute of love. It shows that love puts the best possible construction on the behavior of others. One under the control of love is not censorious, disposed to find fault, or to impute wrong motives to others.
5.zh:
不做害羞的事，不求自己的益處，不輕易發怒，不計算人的惡，

**害羞的事。**aschēmoneo，“不當之舉”，“不光彩之舉”。在七十士譯本中該詞指“裸體”（見結16:7,22等）。愛絕不會鹵莽，粗俗或無理，絕不會傷害別人的感情。基督在世上時很在意人的感受。祂對所有的人都是禮貌得體的（見《傳道良助》121頁）。每一個主的真門徒始終都會表現出謙恭的態度，絕不會順從本能的衝動，表現出粗魯尖刻的無禮態度（見《傳道良助》123頁）。愛總是在尋求正確合宜的事物，處理好生活中的一切關係，因為愛心會努力促進別人的幸福，所以必然會避免一切可能破壞或干擾真快樂的事情。
這裡可能指一些哥林多信徒在公共禮拜或異教宴席上的不當之舉（見林前8:10-12；11:4-6,20-22）。對於基督徒來說，個人的看法，願望和做法應當為愛心所取代，旨在關心別人的舒適、方便和快樂。
愛的合宜之舉消除了一切狂熱失衡的狀態，避免導致情緒失控，羞辱上帝的聖工。愛不做害羞的事，這句話說明愛始終受理智的控制，不光是情緒和情感。單純情感和情緒的反應，並將之誤稱為愛的，並不是出於理智的行動，也不會考慮別人的情緒和感受。
**自己的益處。**與真愛的性質完全相反的是自私地把追求自己的利益、影響或尊榮作為人生的大目標（見10:24,23）。在愛的所有特徵中，這是未蒙潔淨的心最難理解的。人的本性是首先關注自己的。這種關注往往超過其他的一切。但是基督的態度，即愛的態度，是把自己放到最後，把別人放在前面（見太5:43-46；7:12註釋）。人自私的本性進一步證明了罪惡已經完全扭曲了上帝為人類的經驗所制定的秩序，使人將情感和興趣集中在自己身上（見耶17:9；羅7:14-18,20；8:5-8；雅4:4；見太10:39註釋）。一個擁有上帝無私之愛的人忘記了自己，完全關注於遵行上帝的旨意。所以他願意在以愛心服侍他人中捨棄自己的生命（見太22:37-39；徒10:38；《傳道良助》112頁；《教會證言》卷五第9,10頁）。
耶穌“周流四方，行善事”（徒10:38）。這句話說明，人如果單為自己而活，以促進個人利益為人生的主要目標，他就不可能是一個真正的基督徒。基督徒乃是跟隨基督的人。所以他會拒絕內體本性利己的慾望，願意犧牲自己的舒適、光陰、便利、財富和才幹，來促進人類的幸福。
**輕易發怒。**“輕易”一詞是外加的，顯然沒有依據。實際上它會使人誤解這句話的意思。愛不會發怒，無論輕易與否；沒有什麼能破壞完美之愛的平靜，引發煩惱，焦躁和憤怒。加上“輕易”一詞暗示有時允許發洩一定的怒氣和怨恨。但真正的愛並不是這樣（見詩119:165；來12:3；彼前2:23）。基督徒知道自己內心的本性是違背上帝旨意的。他已經把自己交給上帝，向罪而死，所以沒有理由生氣或煩惱。他只用把一切都交給上帝，知道無論發生什麼事，他都在那位為他的利益而掌管萬事的主關愛和監管之下（見羅6:11；8:28；彼前5:6,7）。悔改最顯著的效果之一就是原本急噪易怒的性情發生了變化。在聖靈的影響下，這樣的人變得溫柔、文雅和安靜了。撒但惹他生氣，使他故態復萌一切努力都失敗了。
**不計算人的惡。**原文指不計較過去的錯誤；不追究或指控任何人的過錯。這是愛的又一個美好的基督化特徵。它說明愛要對別人的行為作出最好的解釋。一個為愛所控制的人，不會挑剔找茬，歪曲別人的動機。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《對作者和編輯的勉言》第67頁；《歷代願望》第20，439頁；《早期著作》第112頁；《今日的生活》第84頁；《證言》卷二第276，313頁；《證言》卷三第397頁；《證言》卷五第124頁；《證言》卷七第243頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。見箴16：32懷愛倫註釋；@。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–7節）**。《傳道良助》第448頁。

8.en: Faileth. Gr. ekpiptō, “to fall off [or “from”],” “to fall from its place,” “to fail,” “to perish.” Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading piptō, the simple form of the verb. Genuine love does not fall off like a leaf or a flower (see James 1:11; 1 Peter 1:24). When a flower has given its fragrance and beauty during the hours of sunshine, it has served its purpose, and the cold winds and frosts cause it to wither and fall off the plant. Not so with love. In days of stress and strain, as well as when all is bright and fair, love ever remains the same, shedding its fragrance of trust and hope and faith all around. This must be so, for love is the very foundation of law, and the law of God is eternal (see Ps. 119:160; Matt. 5:17, 18; Luke 16:17). Every believer is enjoined to cultivate this fruit of the Spirit, and every believer may be assured that there can be no experience of life for which love does not make provision; love can be relied on at all times to solve all problems. Prophecies. The gift of prophecy was provided by God for the guidance of the church through the ages (see Ps. 77:20; Hosea 12:13; Rev. 12:17; 19:10). When the need for such guidance no longer exists—that is, when the people of God reach their heavenly home—prophecies will cease. Fail. Gr. katargeō, “to render null,” “to bring to an end,” here used in the passive form, “to be brought to an end.” Tongues. Like prophecy, this gift, which served a useful function in the early church (see Additional Note on Chapter 14), would no longer be required. Cease. Gr. pauō, “to pause,” “to leave off.” Knowledge. Not knowledge in general, but the gift of knowledge, which enabled men to explain the truth clearly and logically to others (see on ch. 12:8). Paul is setting forth the superiority of love over various spiritual gifts that were useful in building up the church, but which, with the church triumphant in the kingdom of glory, will no longer be needed. Shall vanish away. Gr. katargeō (see above under “fail”).
8.zh:
愛是永不止息。先知講道之能終必歸於無有；說方言之能終必停止；知識也終必歸於無有。

**止息。**ekpipto，“衰退”，“從原來的位置落下”，“失敗”，“毀滅”。有文本為pipto，是該動詞的簡單形式。真正的愛不會像樹葉或花朵那樣凋落（見雅1:11；彼前1:24）。在陽光照耀的時候，花朵吐露出它的芳香和豔麗，為它的宗旨服務。寒風和霜凍會使它枯萎凋羅。愛卻不是如此。在緊張和壓迫的日子裡，愛依舊向四周散發出信靠、盼望和信心的香氣，像在陽光燦爛的日子裡一樣。這是必然的，因為愛是律法的基礎，而上帝的律法則是永恆的（見詩119:160；太5:17,18；路16:17）。每一個信徒都要栽培這屬靈的果子；每一個信徒都可以確知，沒有什麼人生的經驗是愛所不能進入的；愛在任何時候都是解決所有問題所必需的。
**先知講道。**先知講道的恩賜是上帝所賜引導歷代教會的（見詩77:20；何12:13；啟12:17；19:10）。當上帝的子民到達他們的天家之後，不再需要這種引導，先知講道的恩賜也就結束了。
**無有。**katargeo，“無效”，“結束”，這裡用的是被動語態。
**說方言。**這個恩賜像先知講道的恩賜一樣，曾在早期的教會里發揮作用，以後將不再需要（見14章補充註釋）。
**停止。**pauo，“中止”。
**知識。**不是一般的知識，而是知識的恩賜，就是清楚而合乎邏輯地向別人解釋真理的能力（見林前12:8註釋）。保羅說明愛要超過用於教會建設的各種屬靈恩賜。但在榮耀的國度裡，勝利的教會將不再需要這些恩賜。
**終必歸於無有。**katargeo（見上面“無有”註釋）。

1.en: Though. Paul has enumerated and defined the place of the gifts of the Spirit in the church (ch. 12). Now he proceeds to show that the possession of all these gifts, and other additional qualities, does not make one a Christian if he does not possess the supreme gift of love. This beautiful prose poem has been called the “greatest, strongest, deepest thing Paul ever wrote” (Harnack). The nature, worth, and eternal duration of love in comparison with the temporary gifts is here set forth. This chapter continues the discussion of the subject introduced in ch. 12, namely, spiritual gifts. Paul has noted the fact that the various spiritual endowments were conferred in such a way as to advance the building up and welfare of the church (see ch. 12:4–28). Now he shows that possession of the gifts mentioned therein, good though it is, can be superseded by an endowment that is more valuable than anything previously described, and that the gift is available to all (cf. Gal. 5:22). 6 Nichol, F. D. (1978). The Seventh-day Adventist Bible Commentary : The Holy Bible with exegetical and expository comment. Commentary Reference Series (1 Co 11:1). Washington, D.C.: Review and Herald Publishing Association. Tongues of men. This may be a reference to the power of utterance that is found in the most highly qualified and gifted orators among men, or to the many different languages used by the nations of this earth. If the speaker lacks love, one of the basic characteristics of God, his superior eloquence or his facility in the use of languages is as valueless for the promotion of the kingdom of God as the meaningless noises of any resonant piece of brass or vainly clanging cymbal (see 1 John 4:8; DA 22; GC 487, 493). Of angels. By this Paul may have referred either to the gift of tongues so highly prized in Corinth (see on ch. 14) or to the elevated language of angels. However, the highly spectacular manifestation of tongues or even the ability to speak with angelic tongue does not confer any honor on the one who receives it, nor is it of any real value to him if it is not associated with love. The apostle designed to correct the wrong evaluation the Corinthians placed upon the gift of tongues and to stimulate them to seek for love as the most valuable endowment. Charity. Gr. agapē, “love,” the higher type of love, which recognizes something of value in the person or object that is loved; love that is based on principle, not on emotion; love that grows out of respect for the admirable qualities of its object. This love is that which is seen between the Father and Jesus (see John 15:10; 17:26); it is the redeeming love of the Godhead for lost humanity (see John 15:9; 1 John 3:1; 4:9, 16); it is the special quality demonstrated in the dealings of Christians with one another (see John 13:34, 35; 15:12–14); it is used to signify the believer’s relation to God (see 1 John 2:5; 4:12; 5:3). Love for God is shown by conformity with His will; this is proof of love (see John 2:4, 5). See Additional Note on Psalm 36; see on Matt. 5:43, 44. The word “charity” is not comprehensive enough to indicate the wide sweep of interest in the well-being of others that is contained in the word agapē. Indeed “charity” may convey a highly restricted idea of welfare aid. The word “love” is better, but that must be understood in the light of all that is said in this chapter concerning it. This “love” (agapē) must not be confused with that which is sometimes called love, a quality composed largely of feeling and emotion that has the center in self and the desires of self. Agapē centers the interest and concern in others and leads to appropriate action. The Corinthian church had been greatly troubled with internal discord resulting in divisions and parties (see ch. 1:11, 12). Some boasted of their superior qualifications and gifts (see chs. 3:3–5, 8, 18, 19, 21; 4:6, 7). This chapter shows that possession of various gifts of the Spirit avails nothing if the individual is devoid of love. Brass. Gr. chalkos, “brass,” or anything made of brass. Here, modified by “sounding,” it probably refers to a gong or a trumpet. The idea is that of a resounding instrument, one that makes a loud noise and gives an appearance of great importance but is merely a lifeless emitter of sound. Tinkling. Gr. alalazō, an onomatopoeic word, originally formed to express the loud yell uttered by an army when rushing into battle. From this original use it came to mean the making of any loud noise, such as a shriek or a wail of lamentation. Here alalazō is used to describe monotonous, clanging sounds of a cymbal.
1.zh:
我若能說萬人的方言，並天使的話語，卻沒有愛，我就成了鳴的鑼，響的鈸一般。

**我若能說。**保羅已經列舉和說明了教會中聖靈恩賜的地位（12章）。現在他接著說明擁有這一切恩賜和其他品質，並不能使人成為基督徒，如果他不具備最高恩賜——愛的話。這首美妙的散文詩被譽為保羅所寫“最偉大，最動情，最深刻”的作品（哈納克）。
本節將愛的性質，價值和永恆性與暫時的恩賜進行比較。本章繼續討論12章的主題，即屬靈的恩賜。保羅注意到各種屬靈的恩賜都是為了促進教會的建設和福利（見12:4-28）。現在他說明，這裡所提到的恩賜雖然很好，但與那更有價值的恩賜相比，就顯得相形見絀了。而那種恩賜是人人都能獲得的（參加5:22）。
**萬人的方言。**可能指人間最有能力和恩賜之演說家的口才，或指世界各民族的不同語言。如果講話的人不具備上帝的基本品格之一——愛，他那出色的口才和駕御語言的能力就像鳴的鈸和響的鑼一樣，無助於上帝國度的推進（見約壹4:8；《歷代願望》22頁；《善惡之爭》487，493頁）。
**天使的話語。**保羅可能是指哥林多所推崇的口才（見林前14章註釋），或天使高貴的語言。但卓越的口才，甚至是天使的語言，若沒有愛，就不能給擁有者增添什麼光彩，也沒有任何真正的價值。使徒想要糾正哥林多信徒對於方言的錯誤認識，鼓勵他們尋求最有價值的恩賜──愛。
**愛（英語charity）。**希臘語為agape，高層次的愛，能欣賞被愛對象的價值。這種愛是以原則為基礎的，不是出於感情的衝動。這種愛是對被愛者高貴品質的尊敬。這是存在於聖父與耶穌之間的愛（見約15:10；17:26）；是上帝對於淪喪人類的救贖之愛（見約15:9；約壹3:1；4:9,16）；是基督徒彼此相待所表現的特殊品質（見約13:34,35；15:12-14）；是用來代表信徒與上帝之間的關係（見約壹2:5；4:12；5:3）。對上帝的愛表現在遵行祂的旨意；這是愛的憑據（見約壹2:4,5）。見《詩篇》36篇補充註釋；見太5:43,44註釋。
英語的“charity”還不足以表達agape一詞所包含對於他人利益的廣泛關注 。它比較侷限物質的幫助。譯為“love”（愛）要好一些，但必須根據本章對愛的詮釋來理解。這“愛”（agape）不要與以自我和自我的願望為中心的情感相混淆。Agape注重關心他人，並導致恰當的行動。
哥林多教會因內部不和導致分門結黨（見1:11,12）而大受侵擾。有人因自己的優點和恩賜而誇口（見3:3-5,8,18,19,21；4:6,7）。本章說明如果沒有愛，單憑擁有聖靈各樣的恩賜算不得什麼。
**鑼。**chalkos，銅或銅製的樂器。用“鳴的”來修飾，可能指銅鑼或銅號，表示一種共鳴的樂器，能發出很響的聲音，表面上看似乎很重要，發出的聲音卻是無生命的。
**響的。**alalazo，擬聲詞，原指軍隊衝入戰場時的吶喊。引申為任何響的聲音，如尖叫或哀鳴。在本節指鈸的啷噹聲。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第560頁；《給管家的勉言》第29頁；《佈道論》第507頁；《證言》卷二第116，581頁；《證言》卷四第133頁；《證言》卷五第98頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–3節）**。《使徒行述》第318頁；《福山寶訓》第38頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《證言》卷五第168頁。

12.en: Through. Rather, “by means of.” Glass. Gr. esoptron, “a mirror.” Another illustration is presented to show the imperfection of the best knowledge that can be obtained on earth. Ancient mirrors consisted of pieces of polished metal (see on Ex. 38:8). The image seen in such mirrors was frequently blurred and dim. Our knowledge of eternal truth is now obscure and dim in comparison with what it will be in heaven. Now our vision is clouded by the infirmities of the physical being, which have their origin in sin; even mental perception is impaired by wrong habits of living, so that spiritual things are only dimly perceived (see 7T 199, 257, 258; 2T 399, 400). Darkly. Gr. en ainigmati, “in a riddle,” “in an enigma,” as in a puzzle where some of the pieces are missing, so that it cannot be properly put together. Such is our present vision of spiritual truth. It is partial, obscure, dim; yet that which can be understood is sufficient to bring joy to the faithful believer as he is enabled to see something of the beauty of the plan that God has made for the redemption and glorification of man. In heaven that which has obscured will be removed and the things that have puzzled men will be made plain; knowledge will increase, and with the increase of knowledge will come ever-increasing joy (see 8T 328). Shall I know. That is, know fully, recognize, acknowledge, understand. The idea of “know fully” is not in the word translated “know,” earlier in the verse. Even as. That is, in the very same manner; not necessarily to the same extent. When the imperfections of this life are all past and that remarkable change has been effected whereby the “corruptible” puts on “incorruption” and “this mortal” puts on “immortality” (ch. 15:52–54), dimness of vision will be replaced by clear sight, with all intervening obstructions removed. There will be face-to-face communion, so that the redeemed believer will, according to his ever-increasing ability, know and understand things fully. I am known. Rather, “I was fully known,” or “I have been fully known,” that is, by God. Although in this life man’s knowledge of God is partial, God’s knowledge of man is complete. The more complete knowledge that man will possess in the world to come is compared with God’s knowledge of man in this present life. However, man’s knowledge will never equal God’s, or even approach it. For this reason the phrase “even as” must not be interpreted as meaning “equal in extent” (see above under “even as”). The words of this verse have sometimes been used to state the truth that in the kingdom of glory God’s people will recognize one another (see DA 804). It should be remembered that this is not Paul’s meaning in this present passage. There will indeed be such a recognition, but the apostle is here speaking of our present perplexities that in the world to come will be explained, and of our imperfect knowledge that will there be made complete (see 5T 706).
12.zh:
我們如今彷彿對著鏡子觀看，糢糊不清（原文作：如同猜謎）；到那時就要面對面了。我如今所知道的有限，到那時就全知道，如同主知道我一樣。

**對著。**或“藉著”。
**鏡子。**esoptron。保羅用另一個比喻來說明人間最好的知識也是不完全的。古時的鏡子是由磨光的金屬製作的（見出38:8註釋）。這種鏡子裡的形象往往模糊不清。我們現在關於永恆真理的知識與將來到了天上相比，也是模糊不清的。我們目前的視線因肉體的軟弱而遮蔽，其根源就是罪。即使我們心靈的觀察能力，也因錯誤的生活習慣而遭到破壞，所以只能隱約地看見屬靈的事物（見《教會證言》卷七第199,257,258頁；《教會證言》卷二第399,400頁）。
**模糊不清。**en ainigmati，“如同猜謎”。一個謎語中有一部分是缺失的，所以不能連貫起來。我們現在對屬靈真理的理解也是如此局部的而模糊不清的。但是已經理解的部分足以給忠心的信徒帶來喜樂，因為他能夠看見上帝救贖和榮耀人類計劃中的美。到了天上，模糊不清的將要除去，疑惑不解的將要明瞭，知識將要增加。隨著知識的增加將是喜樂的不斷增加（見《教會證言》卷八第328頁）。
**全知道。**就是完全認識，理解和明白。本節前面的“知道”並無“全知道”之意。
**如同。**但不一定是相同的程度。當今生的不完美過去之後，將會發生顯著的變化；“必朽壞的”必穿上“不朽壞的”；“必死的”穿上“不死的”（15:52-54）；清晰的圖象將代替模糊不清的畫面；一切阻擋的障礙都將除去。得贖的信徒將要與主面對面交通，隨著不斷增加的能力而完全認識和理解真理。
**主知道我。**即“我被上帝充分了解”。雖然在今生人對上帝的認識是有侷限性的，但上帝對人卻是完全瞭解的。人類在來生的完美知識，將能與在今生上帝對人的瞭解相比。然而人的知識永遠不能與上帝相等或相近。因此“如同”不可理解為“同樣程度”（見上面“如同”註釋）。本節的詞語有時用來表示在榮耀的國度裡上帝的子民相互認識的事實（見《歷代願望》804頁）。務要記住，這不是保羅這段話的原意。確實有這樣的認識存在，但是保羅在本節說的是我們現在的困惑到了來生都將明瞭；我們不完全的知識到了將來都要完全（見《教會證言》卷五第706頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第544頁；《歷代願望》第804頁；《教育論》第303，306頁；《善惡之爭》第676，677頁；《福山寶訓》第27頁；《服務真詮》第466頁；《今日的生活》第12，353，366頁；《拾級就主》第113頁；《救贖的故事》第432頁；《證言》卷一第30頁；《證言》卷三第540頁；《證言》卷五第706頁；《證言》卷六第309頁；《證言》卷八第328頁。

9.en: In part. The gifts of knowledge and prophecy provide only partial glimpses of the inexhaustible treasures of divine knowledge. This limited knowledge will appear to be all but canceled in the superior brightness of the eternal world, as the light of a candle loses its importance when placed in the bright light of the sun.
9.zh:
我們現在所知道的有限，先知所講的也有限，

**有限。**知識和先知講道的恩賜只能讓我們看見一部分上帝知識的無限財富。這有限的知識在無比輝煌的永恆世界面前顯得卻不足道，就像燭光在輝煌的陽光下顯得微不足道一樣。

6.en: Iniquity. Gr. adikia, “unrighteousness.” Love finds no pleasure in any kind of unrighteousness, whether on the part of friend or foe. Unrighteousness, which is sin (see 1 John 5:17), is altogether foreign to the divine nature of love; therefore one who loves cannot be pleased with anything that is not in harmony with the will of God. Love does not rejoice over the vices of others or find happiness because others are found guilty of wrongdoing. It does not take malicious delight in hearing a report that someone has erred (see Prov. 10:12; 11:13; 17:9; 1 Peter 4:8). The unsanctified heart is glad when an enemy falls into sin, or when an opponent makes a mistake that involves him in disgrace, but not so with love. It takes the opposite course, and seeks to help even an enemy when he is in trouble (see Prov. 24:17; 25:21; Matt. 5:44; Rom. 12:20). Only those not sanctified by the truth find pleasure in the wrongdoing of others (see Rom. 1:32; 12:9). Truth. Here “truth” stands in contrast with “iniquity” and means virtue, righteousness, goodness. Love finds pleasure, not in the vices, but in the virtues, of others. Love is interested in the advancement of truth and the happiness of man; therefore it is thankful whenever the cause of truth is sustained (see Mark 9:35–40; Phil. 1:14–18). Love cannot find happiness in sin of any kind or in the punishment meted out to the sinner; rather, it finds pleasure in the liberation of man from the shackles of sin, because such liberation brings him into harmony with truth and makes him a candidate for the happiness of heaven, for which he was created (see Eze. 18:23, 32; 33:11; John 8:32; 17:17; 1 John 4:8; COL 290).
6.zh:
不喜歡不義，只喜歡真理；

**不義。**adikia。愛是不喜歡任何不義的，無論是在仇敵還是朋友身上。不義就是罪（見約壹5:17），與上帝愛的本性是完全不同的；因此有愛心的人不可能喜歡任何不符合上帝旨意的事情。愛不以別人的罪惡為快樂，也不因別人的過錯而高興，不會因聽說有別人犯錯誤而幸災樂禍（見箴10:12；11:13；17:9；彼前4:8）。當敵人犯罪，對手犯錯蒙羞時，未經潔淨的心會高興，但有愛心的人卻不會這樣。反之，他甚至會在仇敵遭難時伸出援手（見箴24:17；25:21；太5:44；羅12:20）。只有那些未因真理成聖的人才會以他人的錯誤為樂（見羅1:32；12:9）。
**真理。**與“不義”相對照，有美德、公義、善良之意。愛心以別人的美德，而不是罪惡為樂。愛心關壞真理的推進和人類的幸福；所以當真理的事業得到維護時，它就總是充滿感恩的（見可9:35-40；腓1:14-18）。
愛心不能在罪人的罪惡和相應的懲罰中得到快樂；它的快樂是在擺脫罪惡束縛的人身上，因為這種解脫使他與真理相和諧，有資格享受天國的快樂。人就是為此而被造的（見結18:23,32；33:11；約8:32；17:17；約壹4:8；《天路》290頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》第279頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–8節）**。《證言》卷五第169頁。

2.en: Prophesy. The apostle moves on to the more important, though possibly less sensational, gift of speaking as God’s inspired messenger, passing along instruction from Heaven to the church. The superiority of this gift over tongues and other spiritual gifts is emphasized in ch. 14:1, 39. The prophet, who stands between God and men and reveals God’s will to men, must be dominated by love, otherwise his messages will have little effect upon the hearers. Mysteries. Gr. mustēria (see on Matt. 13:11; Rom. 11:25). Because of sin, man’s powers of mind have become weakened; his capability of understanding the wonders of life, both natural and spiritual, is greatly inferior to that which God originally intended him to have (see Isa. 6:9, 10; John 12:37–40; 2 Cor. 4:4; 4T 585; 5T 698, 701). Long and arduous study and research are required to enable men to discover the secrets of nature, but these were readily acquired by Adam before he sinned (see PP 50, 51). The unconverted, sin-dominated mind cannot understand the things of God. This is because sin has wrought a complete change in man’s spiritual nature, so that his ways are diametrically opposed to those of his Creator (see Isa. 55:8, 9). To the prophets God sees fit to reveal the workings of His will on behalf of men. In turn, they are commissioned to instruct men as to their relation to God and their fellow men (see Ps. 25:14; Amos 3:7). Knowledge. By “knowledge” Paul doubtless refers, not to knowledge in general, but to the gift of knowledge described in ch. 12:8 as “the word of knowledge,” meaning “the utterance of knowledge” (see comment there; cf. on ch. 12:28). Faith. That is, the gift of faith described in ch. 12:9 (see comment there). Charity. See on v. 1. Nothing. Having listed the possible possession of the gifts of prophecy, wisdom, knowledge, and faith, outstanding and greatly desired spiritual endowments, Paul makes the simple statement that all these things, admirable and important though they may be, are ineffective without love. The same is true also of acquired gifts, such as intellectual attainments. Satan has great intellectual power, and knowledge that exceeds that of men, but he is not elevated thereby (see 2T 171; PP 36; 5T 504). The mind that is not surrendered to Christ and actuated by His Spirit is under the control of Satan, who works in it to accomplish his own pleasure (see 5T 515). Thus it becomes apparent that mere intellectual attainments, separated from the Godlike quality of love, merely serve to aid the enemy in achieving his ends, and do nothing to further the spiritual interests of men (see 1 John 4:8). One who may have had much of this world’s wisdom, together with a theoretical understanding of the relationship that should exist between man and God, and yet had no experimental knowledge of love, would still be lost. His efforts to do good to others would be fruitless, and the great goal that should be his in life, the glorification of God, would remain unreached (see John 4:7, 8; MB 37).
2.zh:
我若有先知講道之能，也明白各樣的奧秘，各樣的知識，而且有全備的信，叫我能夠移山，卻沒有愛，我就算不得什麼。

**先知講道。**使徒接著講到那比較重要，但又不那麼顯眼的恩賜，就是作上帝感召的使者，向教會傳達天上的指示。14:1,39強調這個恩賜勝過說方言和其他的恩賜。先知是站在上帝和人類之間向人傳達上帝旨意的，必須為愛所支配，否則他的信息在聽眾身上就收效甚微。
**奧秘。**mustēria（見太13:11；羅11:25註釋）。人的思維能力因罪而減弱。他對於自然和屬靈生命中奇蹟的理解力遠遠達不到上帝當初對他的旨意（見賽6:9,10；約12:37-40；林後4:4；《教會證言》卷五第698,701頁）。人類經過長期艱辛學習研究才發現自然秘密，亞當在犯罪以前早已瞭解（見《先祖與先知》50，51頁）。未悔改而被罪惡所控制的心是無法理解上帝之事的。因為罪完全改變了人的屬靈特質，以致他的思維方式與創造主的旨意完全相反（見賽55:8,9）。上帝認為先知可以傳達祂為對於人類旨意的作為。於是他們奉命教導人有關他們與上帝的關係，以及他們與同胞的關係（見詩25:14；摩3:7）。
**知識。**保羅所說的“知識”無疑不是一般的知識，而是林前12:8所描述“知識的言語”的恩賜（見該節註釋；參林前12:28註釋）。
**信。**指林前12:9所描述信心的恩賜（見該節註釋）。
**愛。**見第1節註釋。
**算不得什麼。**保羅列舉了先知講道，智慧，知識和信心等令人羨慕的出色的屬靈恩賜之後，簡要地指出，這一切恩賜雖然重要且令人羨慕，若沒有愛就沒有效果。
已經獲得的恩賜，比如學識，也是如此。撒但有很高的智力和超人的知識，但不可因此而抬舉他（見《教會證言》卷二第171頁；《先祖與先知》36頁；《教會證言》卷五第504頁）。不降服基督並受祂的靈控制的人就是受撒但控制的。撒但在他心中工作，就是要實現他自己的意願（見《教會證言》卷五第515頁）。因此單有學識卻沒有基督化的愛，就只能幫助仇敵達到他的目的，對於人類屬靈的利益毫無促進（見約壹4:8）。一個人可以具有有豐富的屬世智慧，在理論上知道人與上帝之間的關係，卻沒有愛的實際知識，他依然會淪喪。他努力為別人行善也沒有用處。他本應達到的人生偉大目標，就是榮耀上帝，卻未能達到（見約壹4:7,8；《福山寶訓》37頁）。

3.en: Bestow. Gr. psōmizō, “to feed by putting bits of food into the mouth,” “to dole out,” “to feed out in morsels”; used in the NT only here and in Rom. 12:20. Here the word may apply to the distribution of goods to the poor in small portions. It was probably customary in Paul’s day for the wealthy to dole out alms to the poor at the gate of their property (see Luke 16:20, 21). Then, too, they probably distributed alms in small portions to many people so that there would be a larger number benefited and ready to praise the donor. Almsgiving was considered to be a great virtue, and was frequently done ostentatiously. Jesus severely reproved this desire for popular acclaim (see on Matt. 6:1– 4). To emphasize the vanity of such false charity, Paul pointed out that if all that a man possessed was thus doled out and yet true love was absent from the life, it would all be empty hypocrisy and of no value spiritually. Though such behavior might result in good to others, it could not meet with God’s approval because the requisite character qualifications were lacking. To be burned. Important textual evidence may also be cited (cf. p. 10) for the reading, “so that I might boast.” With this reading the meaning of the passage is, “though I dole out all my possessions to feed the poor, and though I give over my body, in order that I might boast, it profiteth me nothing.” The idea of the KJV reading is that martyrdom that is sought for self-glorification has no merit. In Paul’s day it was not customary to put men to death by burning; stoning, crucifixion, or beheading with the sword were the usual methods of execution. The question arises: Why, then, would Paul refer to martyrdom by burning? The answer is: Perhaps because burning represents one of the most painful forms of death. To give one’s body to be burned would represent an extreme form of self-sacrifice. Some have regarded this passage as prophetic of the fearful torture by fire that befell the church in the time of Nero and later. They thus see in the passage a warning against the delusion that merit might be obtained by needlessly seeking martyrdom by fire. Profiteth me nothing. If the one who suffers martyrdom by fire does not possess the character qualifications represented by “love” (agapē), he has no hope of eternal life, and consequently has lost everything. Love, therefore, is more precious and valuable than the gifts of the Spirit that the Corinthians desired to have (vs. 1, 2), or than singular acts of beneficence or self-sacrifice. Nothing can take the place of love. God accepts only the service of love (see John. 14:15, 21, 23; 15:9, 10, 12, 14; 1 John 4:11, 12, 16–21; 5:1–3).
3.zh:
我若將所有的賙濟窮人，又捨己身叫人焚燒，卻沒有愛，仍然於我無益。

**賙濟。**psōmizo，“把一點食物喂入口中”，“救濟”，“少量餵養”；該詞在《新約》中只出現在本節和羅12:20，在這裡表示把少量的物資分給窮人，可能指保羅時代財主在家門口向窮人施捨的風俗（見路16:20,21）。他們小額的佈施，是為了一大批人受益，從而稱讚捐贈者。施捨被視為美德，故常常有人為炫耀而行善。耶穌嚴厲譴責這種譁眾取寵的行為（見太6:1-4註釋）。保羅為了強調這種假慈善的虛偽，就指出，如果一個人捐獻了他的所有，但他的生活中沒有真愛，那仍是偽善，毫無屬靈的價值。這樣的行為雖然可能對別人有好處，卻不能蒙上所悅納，因為缺乏必要品格特徵。
**叫人焚燒。**有文本為“為了誇口”。若是這樣，本句就成了“我若將所有的賙濟窮人，又捨己身，為了誇口，仍然與我無益”。
這句話的意思是，為榮耀自己而殉身是毫無價值的。在保羅的時代，並沒有用火刑處死人的習慣。死刑的常用方式是用石頭打死，釘十字架，或用劍斬首。有人要問：那為什麼保羅要提到焚身殉難呢？回答是：因為焚身可能代表一種最痛苦的死亡方式。捨己焚身代表自我犧牲的極端形式。有人認為這句話是預言尼祿時代以及後來臨到教會可怕的火刑苦難。他們就這樣從這句話中看到警告：不要誤以為焚身殉難有功勞可稱。
**與我無益。**焚身殉難如果沒有“愛”（agape）的品質，就沒有永生的盼望，最終將喪失一切。因此，愛的價值要勝過哥林多信徒所希望得到的種種聖的恩賜（1,2節），也勝過單純的慈善和自我犧牲的行為。愛是無法替代的。上帝只接受愛的侍奉（見約14:15,21,23；15:9,10,12,14；約壹4:11,12,16-21；5:1-3）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷二第116頁；《證言》卷四第133頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–7節）**。《證言》卷二第169頁。

4.en: Suffereth long. In vs. 4–7 Paul proceeds to analyze love. He points out seven excellent characteristics of love and eight acts and attitudes that are totally foreign to its nature. In this eulogy he sets forth the superior quality of love in both its positive and its negative aspect. The personification of love in these verses heightens the beauty of the description, for Paul ascribes to love those characteristics that are found in all who truly love. Throughout the paragraph occasional glimpses are seen of the faults in the church at Corinth that were in direct contrast to the excellent qualities of love. Forbearance, or long-suffering, in a world where impatience and intolerance prevail, is a precious attribute. Love bears long with the faults, failings, and weaknesses of others. It recognizes that all human beings are fallible, and that, therefore, due allowance must be made for manifestations of the outworking of errors that result from man’s inherently sinful nature. Long-suffering is opposed to haste, to passionate expressions and thoughts, and to irritability. This word denotes the state of mind that enables a man to be patiently quiet and to bear long when oppressed, wrongfully accused, and persecuted (see Eph. 4:2; Col. 3:12; 2 Tim. 4:2; 2 Peter 3:15; cf. Matt. 26:63; 27:12, 14; see on Matt. 5:10–12). He who is long-suffering possesses one of the fruits of the Spirit (see Gal. 5:22). Is kind. Gr. chrēsteuomai, “to be gentle,” “to exercise kindness,” “to be considerate and mild.” The word portrays the gracious nature of one who is actuated by the Spirit of God, one who is ever seeking to reveal by word and deed an understanding sympathy for, and appreciation of, the struggles and difficulties of others. The idea of the word is that under all circumstances of life, whether harsh and provoking, painful or sorrowful, love is mild and gentle. Love is the reverse of hatred, which manifests itself in severity, anger, harshness, unkindness, and revenge. A man who really loves another is kind to him, anxious to do him good, gentle and courteous, because he does not wish to hurt his feelings, but seeks to promote his happiness (see 1 Peter 3:8). Envieth. Gr. zēloō, “to be zealous,” either in a good or bad sense; here in a bad sense, “to be envious,” that is, to exhibit wrong or unpleasant feelings toward others on account of advantages possessed by them. Such feelings give rise to strife and division, entirely contrary to the teachings of Jesus, for He exhorted men to love one another and live together in unity (see John 15:12; 17:22; 1 John 3:23). Envy, or jealousy, is one of the most cruel and contemptible of all human failings (see Prov. 27:4; Song of Sol. 8:6). Lucifer, the exalted angel who was privileged to be one of the covering cherubs by the throne of God, was overcome by envy and lost his high position (see Isa. 14:12–15; Eze. 28:14, 15). Since his fall, Satan has sought to implant his own dreadful vice of envy in the heart of every human being, so that all may be ruined, as he was. Only love can drive out jealousy. However, contentedness with what the Lord has permitted us to have does not debar us from desiring earnestly the best gifts and longing ardently for the “more excellent way” of love, which is described in this chapter (see 1 Cor. 12:31). Vaunteth … itself. Gr. perpereuomai, “to be vainglorious,” “to boast oneself.” Love does not sound its own praises; it is humble and does not try to exalt self. One in whose heart true love is found remembers the life and death of Jesus and instantly repels every thought or suggestion that would lead to self-glorification (see EW 112, 113). The love that is a gift of the Spirit looks upon every good thing as coming from God and bestowed by Him, and hence there is no ground for vain boasting because of possessing a certain gift from God. Is … puffed up. Gr. phusioō, “to puff up,” “to blow up,” “to inflate,” metaphorically, “to make proud.” Phusioō comes from phusa, “bellows.” Love does not inflate a person with vanity; it does not produce a condition of conceit and self-exaltation. This expression points to the subjective state of pride and self-satisfaction that so often mark those possessed of superior knowledge and abilities (see ch. 8:1). Love does not indulge in mental self-esteem, laying claim to having the best gifts, and in that way ministering to vainglory. Love does not produce ideas of self-importance, nor seek the flattery of others for anything that has been accomplished (see 5T 124).
4.zh:
愛是恆久忍耐，又有恩慈；愛是不嫉妒；愛是不自誇，不張狂，

**恆久忍耐。**保羅在4-7節中對愛進行了分析。他指出愛的七個優秀特徵和八種與愛的性質完全相悖的行為與態度。在這首頌歌中，他從正面和反面描述了愛的美好特點。這幾節對愛的擬人化描寫，更體現了愛的美感，因為保羅把所有真有愛心的人的特徵都歸諸於愛。從這段文字中，我們隱約可見哥林多教會的缺點，與愛的優秀品質有迥然之別。
在這個浮躁和不寬容的世界裡，恆久忍耐是一種寶貴的品質。愛能長久容忍別人的缺點，失敗和軟弱。它承認全人類都可能犯錯，因此應當寬容那因罪的本性所引起的錯誤行為。恆久忍耐是與急躁，衝動和易怒相反的。該詞表示一個人在遭到壓制，誣告和逼迫時保持安靜和長久容忍的心態（見弗4:2；西3:12；提後4:2；彼後3:15；參太26:63；27:12,14；見太5:10-12註釋）。恆久忍耐的人擁有一樣聖靈所結的果子（見加5:22）。
**有恩慈。**chrēsteuomai，“溫柔”，“仁慈”，“考慮周到”。該詞表示上帝的靈所激發的高尚品質，對別人的掙扎和難處始終表現出同情和理解的言行。該詞的意思是，在任何生活的環境中，無論是艱辛危難，還是痛苦悲哀，總是表現出溫柔親切的愛。與愛相反的是恨，表現在嚴酷、惱怒、尖刻、無情和報復上。一個真正愛別人的人會仁慈待人，熱心溫柔謙恭地為其謀利，因為他不願傷害那人的感情，而是設法增進他的快樂（見彼前3:8）。
**嫉妒。**zēloō，該詞用於褒義時有“熱心”之意，但本節用於貶義，指對別人的長處表現出不悅或惡意。這種情緒會引起爭執和分裂，與耶穌的教訓完全相反，因為耶穌勸人要彼此相愛，合而為一（見約15:12；17:22；約壹3:23）。嫉妒是人類最殘酷卑鄙的弱點（見箴27:4；歌8:6）。路錫甫本是高貴的天使，為遮蔽上帝寶座的基路伯之一，卻因妒忌而喪失了崇高的地位（見賽14:12-15；結28:14,15）。撒但墮落以後，設法將自己可怕的忌妒品性灌輸到每一個人心中，使所有的人都像他那樣毀滅。只有愛才能驅散忌妒。但滿足於上帝所賜已經給我們的恩賜，並不妨礙我們熱心追求那上好的恩賜，急切盼望那“更大的恩賜”（見林前12:31），就是本章中所描寫的愛。
**自誇。**perpereuomai。愛是不自誇的；它謙卑而不張揚。真有愛心的人始終記住耶穌的生和死，時刻抑制每一個自誇的念頭（見《早期著作》112，113頁）。作為聖靈恩賜的愛把一切美好的事物都看作從上帝而來的，由上帝所賜的，所以沒有理由因擁有某種上帝的恩賜而自誇。
**張狂。**phusioo，喻指“驕傲”。Phusioo源於phusa（“風箱”）。愛不會使人虛妄和自高自大。“張狂”指那些擁有優越知識能力的人所經常表現出來驕傲自滿的心態（見8:1）。愛不會縱容自負之念，說自己擁有上好的恩賜，以滿足他的虛榮心。愛不會自以為了不起，要別人為他的成就而奉承他（見《教會證言》卷五第124頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第114頁；《基督教育原理》第279頁；《今日的生活》第179，334頁；《證言》卷四第65頁；《證言》卷五第123頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《使徒行述》第543頁；《歷代願望》第549頁；《基督教育原理》第283頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–7節）**。《證言》卷四第257頁；《證言》卷五第290頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–8節）**。《使徒行述》第319頁；《教育論》第242頁；《福山寶訓》第16頁。

11.en: Other. Gr. allos, “another [of the same kind],” “one more” (see on Gal. 1:6). There is only one Saviour. Others whom men proclaim as saviors are not “another of the same kind.” They are not saviors at all (see John 14:6; Acts 4:12). Is laid. Or, “is lying.”
11.zh:
因為那已經立好的根基就是耶穌基督，此外沒有人能立別的根基。

**此外。**llos，“同類中的另一位”（見加1:6註釋）。救主只有一位。人所宣稱的其他救主並不是“同類中的另一位”。他們根本不是救主。（見約14:6；徒4:12）。
**立。**或“正在立”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第475頁；《基督教育之研究》第62頁；《歷代願望》第413頁；《教育論》第30頁；《傳道良助》第307頁；《福山寶訓》第149頁；《證言》卷二第145頁；《證言》卷五第270頁；《證言》卷八第297頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–13節）**。《先知與君王》第409頁；《證言》卷三第444頁；《證言》卷四第318頁；《論福利工作》第155頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–15節）**。《使徒行述》第599頁；《基督教育之研究》第222頁；《證言》卷一第125頁。

9.en: Labourers together with God. The Greek places the emphasis on “God.” The work is God’s. Men are merely the hands of the heavenly agencies. As workers in association with the great Master Workman, men must be willing to labor in His way even though that may be altogether contrary to their natural ideas (Col. 3:23).
